The gate takes the holder's symbol text, or the local remainder, from a file on disk or from hook payloads (working-tree form). It writes the result with `git hash-object -w --stdin`, the natural plumbing call for 'write this blob', and commits it into the tree that is pushed to refs/cowork/<b>/code.
findings.consequence: Without --path, git applies no attributes: the blob contains `API_KEY = "REAL-SECRET-VALUE-0123456789"` with CRLF line endings. It is pushed to every collaborator and remains in the host's object store after the next reset. Offsets also disagree between the forms: in the same file 'def use_key' sits at byte 53 in the working tree and byte 35 in the blob, so an offset taken from one form cuts the other in the wrong place.
findings.evidence_detail: sweep/region/git1 (git1_check.sh): autocrlf=true, '*.py text=auto', 'cfg.py filter=secret' (sed clean). `git hash-object -w --stdin < cfg.py` -> blob shows REAL-SECRET-VALUE and ^M. With `--path=cfg.py` -> __REDACTED__ and LF. serve.py fixture: working tree 125,709 bytes, blob 119,749 (BOM kept, 5,960 CR removed). Summarized in extra_results.json git_stored_form. A related but separate failure is a filter that fails open in `git add` (sibling e1/F6).
findings.mitigation: Rule: splice and withdrawal inputs are only blobs read by OID from git: TIP, LAST_APPLIED, and the private-index snapshot, which already passed clean+eol. No working-tree or hook-payload bytes ever enter a blob except through `git add` in the private index or `hash-object --path=<path>`. Write gate outputs with `hash-object -w --stdin --no-filters` only when the input is provably stored-form. A tripwire runs before any push: every line of an output blob must appear in at least one of its input blobs (catches injected plaintext and CRLF). For paths that have a filter attribute, region-level withdrawal is disabled: whole-file hold only.
findings.test: Integration test with a file:// remote: filter-protected file plus CRLF working tree; holder claims a function in it; requester edits that function and another function. Assert that `git cat-file -p` of every pushed blob never contains the plaintext token, that its line endings equal the TIP blob's, and that the tripwire fires (push of that file withheld) when the test deliberately feeds working-tree text into the splice routine.

findings.title: A '#n' ordinal depends on code outside the symbol: a same-named def inserted above makes the gate splice the holder's function over the requester's new code
findings.scenario: The holder holds parse#1, resolved on its own tree, and edits its body. Within the propagation window, or as a human edit that no hook gates, the requester adds two typing @overload stubs named parse above it. In the requester's tree the stubs become parse#1 and #2 and the real function becomes parse#3. The push gate maps the insertion hunk to parse#1/#2 and flags a conflict with the holder's parse#1. It then splices TIP's parse#1 (the holder's real function) over OUT's parse#1 (the first stub). Same pattern in JS: the holder holds the setter `Store.value#1` and the requester adds a getter `get value()` above it. Python platform branches: the holder holds the POSIX `open_console#2` and the requester adds a darwin elif branch above it.
findings.consequence: Silent corruption that parses cleanly. Python: the holder's function now exists twice (real_parse_bodies_after=2) and one of the requester's stubs is deleted. JS: the setter twice, the getter gone. Branches: the darwin variant's body is replaced with the POSIX body. All of it is pushed to every peer. A purely additive edit is also wrongly flagged as a conflict and queued to the holder. Afterwards, a third peer's edit to the holder's real function maps to parse#3, which nobody holds, so the claim no longer protects it.
findings.evidence_detail: results_all.json S3_ordinal_shift.py_overload_stubs (gate_false_conflict=true; splice extra_lines=5 missing_lines=2 parses_clean=true; third_peer_edit_of_holders_function_maps_to='f:def:parse#3'), .js_getter_above_setter (setters_after=2, getters_after=0), .py_platform_branches (missing 'return "/bin/zsh"'). Line-tracked alternative: conflicting_hunks=[] and byte_equal=true for py and js.
findings.mitigation: Rule: claims are matched across peers by (claimCommit OID, stored-form line ranges). The name key (path+kind+qualname+#n) is a display label only and never used for cross-peer matching or splicing. The holder republishes its line ranges with every push. Peers map them forward from claimCommit to TIP through `git diff -U0 claimCommit TIP`: an insertion before lo shifts both bounds, an insertion strictly inside extends hi, a change after hi is ignored. Conflict = a local hunk overlapping a mapped range; a pure insertion counts only if it falls strictly inside (lo <= after_line < hi). Withdrawal = drop the overlapping hunks (see design change on pre-merge withdrawal). The same mapping serves the PreToolUse deny check: map old_string to a line in LAST_APPLIED, then compare with each claim's range mapped into the same commit. Otherwise the deny-at-edit path stays name-keyed and keeps the false block.
findings.test: Use the S3 fixtures (Python overload stubs, JS getter-above-setter, platform branches) as a regression suite. For each, assert no conflict is raised, the pushed blob equals the clean 3-way merge byte for byte, and a third peer's edit inside the holder's real function IS denied. Add the forward-mapping fixtures (fwd_results.json: a 22-line insertion far above, directly above, directly after, and after-with-same-tail; mapped range == true range in all 4).

findings.title: `<toplevel after=X>` keys break when X is renamed (claim bypass) or deleted (two runs merge into one, and the splice deletes a third party's claimed work)
findings.scenario: (a) H holds `<toplevel after=setup_routes>` (three app.add_route lines) and edits the /parse line. The requester renames setup_routes to configure_routes, a legal unclaimed edit, and also edits the /orders line in the claimed block. (b) Peer C holds `<toplevel after=const:app>` (the single line `app.debug = False`). The requester deletes setup_routes and edits app.debug. The run after const:app and the run after setup_routes now touch and form one 6-line region `<toplevel after=const:app>`. The gate splices TIP's 1-line region over it.
findings.consequence: (a) In OUT the holder's key resolves to nothing. The gate sees `<toplevel after=configure_routes>`, which nobody holds, so the requester's edit to claimed lines is pushed. (b) The splice deletes the three add_route lines (5 lines including blanks), including H's claimed and edited `app.add_route("/parse", parse, methods=["POST"])`. H's work disappears from everyone's tree, and nothing queues it because the gate believes it only withdrew the requester's change. The file still parses.
findings.evidence_detail: results_all.json S4_toplevel_after_X: rename_X_only.holder_claim_resolves_in_OUT=false; rename_X_and_edit_claimed_lines.gate_detects_conflict=false (merge_conflicts=0), line_tracked byte_equal=true; delete_X_runs_coalesce: region [5350,5350] in TIP vs [5350,5355] in OUT, splice missing_lines=5 incl. the /parse line, parses_clean=true. guard_results.json flags it (G6 invented hunk). The first S4b attempt edited adjacent lines and hit the adjacent-line merge conflict (sibling e5), so the fixture was spaced by one line.
findings.mitigation: Rule: pseudo-symbol regions (<toplevel>, <imports>, const:, non-code blocks) are claimed and matched only as line ranges, never by their neighbour-derived name. A splice that would delete lines present in both TIP and OUT is forbidden: the gate is a hunk filter (output = TIP plus a subset of the diff(TIP,OUT) hunks), never a region overwrite. The tripwire 'every withdrawn hunk overlaps a foreign claim range, and diff(TIP,output) is a subset of diff(TIP,OUT)' holds the file on violation.
findings.test: Fixture with const:app, app.debug, setup_routes and a 3-line add_route block. (1) Rename setup_routes, edit a claimed line: assert the edit is withdrawn and queued and the rename is pushed. (2) Delete setup_routes and edit app.debug while C holds app.debug: assert the add_route lines are byte-identical in the pushed blob, only the app.debug edit is queued, and the deletion is pushed.

findings.title: git's 3-way merge silently moves a requester's edit of the claimed function's last lines into a new adjacent function with the same tail, so no claim check ever sees it
findings.scenario: H holds compute_total (claimCommit C). Peer D pushes compute_tax, inserted right after compute_total; its last lines (`if discount: / total -= discount / return total` plus blanks) are identical to compute_total's. Requester B, working from LAST_APPLIED = base, edits compute_total's `return total` to `return round(total, 2)`. B's daemon runs merge-tree(LAST_APPLIED, SNAPSHOT, TIP=C+D).
findings.consequence: merge-tree --write-tree and merge-file both exit 0 with identical output: `return round(total, 2)` lands in compute_tax, D's new function, and compute_total is unchanged. The gate inspects diff(TIP,OUT), sees only an edit in unclaimed compute_tax, and pushes it. B's intended change is gone without being queued, D's function is silently altered, and H's claim was useless. Forward-mapping the claim range was correct here; the identity of the hunk was lost inside the merge.
findings.evidence_detail: premerge_results.json and the inspection run: merge-file and merge-tree (real repo in sweep/region/tmp/mt) produce the same blob, exit 0, key_at('return round(total, 2)')='f:def:compute_tax#1'. fwd_results.json D_inserts_after_K_same_tail: mapped range == true range, withdrawn_hunks=[], byte_equal=false (extra 'return round(total, 2)', missing 'return total'). The other three D-insertion variants are byte-correct. The post-merge identity check flags it (symbol_in_SNAP=compute_total#1, symbol_in_OUT=compute_tax#1). Pre-merge withdrawal: byte_equal=true, compute_tax untouched.
findings.mitigation: Rule: the claim check and withdrawal run BEFORE the merge, in LAST_APPLIED coordinates. Map each foreign claim range from its claimCommit into LAST_APPLIED; if claimCommit is not related to LAST_APPLIED by ancestry, hold the whole file. Remove the overlapping local hunks of diff(LAST_APPLIED, SNAPSHOT) into the queue to get SNAPSHOT', then merge SNAPSHOT'. After the merge, run an identity check: for every kept local hunk, the symbol enclosing its text in SNAPSHOT (computed locally) must equal the symbol enclosing the same text in OUT. If not, do not apply or push that file; treat it as a merge conflict for that file. Both checks run on this peer's own trees, so no cross-peer key agreement is needed.
findings.test: Regression fixture from fwd.py/premerge.py: H holds K, D inserts a same-tail function after K, B edits K's last line. Assert the pushed blob leaves compute_tax byte-identical to D's version and B's K edit appears in the queue. Second variant with no claims at all: assert the identity check holds the file instead of pushing the misplaced edit.

findings.title: A claimed function moved by its holder (same file or another file) yields duplicated code or an unclaimed copy
findings.scenario: Same file: H moves compute_total to the end of the file and edits it; requester B edits its last line at the old location. The 3-way merge reports a conflict (exit 1). A daemon that resolves conflicts with --ours or --union, or keeps B's side for a 'blocked' hunk, ends up with compute_total twice: #1 at the old location (B's edit) and #2 at the end (H's). The gate splices TIP's compute_total#1 (the moved function) over OUT's #1. Other file: H moves compute_total from a.py to b.py; the claim key carries path a.py.
findings.consequence: Same file: after the splice the holder's version exists twice (10 duplicated lines), the file parses, and the duplicate goes to everyone. Python's last-definition-wins semantics hide it until someone edits the 'wrong' copy. Other file: a.py:def:compute_total#1 no longer exists in TIP, and b.py:def:compute_total#1 is held by nobody, so B can edit the moved function freely, and B's conflicted a.py hunk can resurrect a stale copy in a.py.
findings.evidence_detail: results_all.json S2_move.same_file: merge_conflicts=1, defs_in_OUT_ours=2, defs_in_OUT_union=2, splice_K1_into_OUT_ours extra_lines=10, parses_clean=true, defs_after_splice=2. other_file: a_py_merge_conflicts=1, key_in_tip_a=false, key_in_tip_b=true. guard_results.json: flagged (G6=1, G7=1). `--union` silently producing broken code was also seen by sibling e5.
findings.mitigation: Rules: (1) Region code never consumes a merge result that had conflicts. A conflicted path is held whole-file (not applied, not pushed), and its local hunks are queued against the holder. No --ours, --union or -X resolution feeds the gate. (2) The holder's PostToolUse detects a move when a claimed range is deleted and a block with the same qualname and at least 80% similar lines appears elsewhere in the same edit batch or file set. It republishes the claim as line ranges at the new (path, lines) and keeps a tombstone range on the old path until the next save. (3) Duplicate-definition tripwire: if any (path, kind, qualname) count in the output exceeds its count in both TIP and OUT, hold the file.
findings.test: Fixtures: move within file plus a requester edit, and move to another file plus a requester edit. Assert nothing is pushed for the conflicted path, the requester's hunk is queued to the holder, the moved function's claim denies the requester's PreToolUse edit at the new location, and no pushed blob ever contains two definitions of compute_total.

findings.title: Multi-range overload-group claims cannot be spliced: span mode deletes unrelated members, pairwise mode duplicates overloads, and partial classes in other files escape the group
findings.scenario: The group key Shop.Billing.OrderService.Calc covers 3 non-contiguous ranges, and the group crosses two `partial class` declarations in the same file (lines 12-15, 24-28, 33-36; class 1 ends at 29, class 2 starts at 31). (a) H adds Calc(int,int); requester B edits Calc(string) (in the window) and Reset() (not claimed). Span splice: OUT[first member start .. last member end] is replaced with TIP's span. (b) B instead inserts a new overload Calc(decimal) after Calc(string). Pairwise splice: OUT has 5 members, TIP has 4, paired by index. (c) Svc.Part2.cs declares Calc(long) in another partial part.
findings.consequence: (a) B's `Log("reset")` change in Reset() is silently reverted and not queued, because it lies inside the span but outside the claim, so the work is lost. (b) Calc(double) appears twice, which is error CS0111 (duplicate member) for every peer. tree-sitter reports parses_clean=true, so only the compiler notices. (c) Part2's overload has a different key (Svc.Part2.cs:group:...Calc#1), so the claimed group's overload set can change underneath the holder.
findings.evidence_detail: results_all.json S6_csharp_overloads: add_overload_span reset_change_survives=false, missing 'Log("reset");'; requester_inserts_overload_pairwise calc_double=2, parses_clean=true; partial_other_file_keys. Line-tracked: add_overload_line_tracked byte_equal=true. guard_results.json flags span(a) G7=1 and pairwise(b) G6=1. Limitation: for (b) in span mode, G7=1 because an overload appended after the last member's line is outside every tracked member range.
findings.mitigation: Rules: (1) A multi-range key is never spliced as text. Each member's line range is tracked and filtered separately (hunk filter). (2) Group membership is checked by name on inserted text: a local insertion hunk whose new text declares a member with the group's simple name, in a declaration of the same type, counts as touching the group. This check is local to OUT and needs no cross-peer agreement. (3) Group claims enumerate every partial declaration of the type across the repo, using a `git grep -n 'partial (class|struct|record) <Name>'` index refreshed per TIP, and publish ranges for each (path, range). If the enumeration fails, the claim covers the whole of every partial file. (4) The C# CS0111 risk is reported as a soft semantic conflict to the holder.
findings.test: With the S6 fixtures: (a) assert Reset's edit is pushed and only the Calc(string) hunk is queued; (b) assert Calc(decimal)'s insertion is queued and the pushed file has exactly one Calc(double); (c) assert a PreToolUse edit adding Calc(string) in Svc.Part2.cs while the group is held is denied or soft-warned. Compile the pushed C# with `dotnet build` in CI to catch CS0111.

findings.title: Sub-block claims inside huge functions resolve to the wrong block after a peer adds or removes one blank line; text-hash anchors are ambiguous and self-invalidating
findings.scenario: A 3,069-line function contains 800 blank-line blocks with realistic repeated shapes. The holder claims block #150, whose text is `result.append(total) / acc.clear()`. Far above it, a peer inserts one blank line in block 20, splitting that block. The gate resolves the claim by ordinal and splices the holder's block. Variants: the peer inserts a blank line inside the claimed block; anchoring is by text hash or by the hash of the first line.
findings.consequence: Ordinal: claim #150 now points at the block starting with `if total > LIMIT:`. The splice writes the holder's block over it, so `alerts.append(("한도", 148))` and `if total > LIMIT:` are lost and `result.append(total)` / `acc.clear()` are duplicated. It parses cleanly and is pushed to all. Text hash: the claimed block's text is identical to 133 other blocks, and the holder's own first edit changes the hash. A blank line inserted inside the claimed block leaves no hash match (132 false matches), and the ordinal resolves to a prefix only.
findings.evidence_detail: results_all.json S9_subblocks: function_lines=3069, n_blocks=800, blocks_with_identical_text_to_claimed=133, requester_split_block20.ordinal_150_now_first_line='if total > LIMIT:', ordinal_splice_after_requester_split extra_lines=2 missing_lines=2 parses_clean=true, blank_inserted_inside_claimed_block.ordinal_150_text_is_prefix_only=true, holder_own_edit_changes_block_hash=true; line_tracked_far_split byte_equal=true.
findings.mitigation: Rule: sub-block claims, like all claims, are stored-form line ranges forward-mapped by diff. Ordinals and content hashes are never identity. A hash may only be a verification field: the published range's text hash at claimCommit, checked after mapping, with whole-symbol escalation if it fails. Sub-block boundaries are fixed when the claim is taken, then follow the lines; they are not recomputed from blank lines on other peers.
findings.test: With the S9 generator (800 blocks): random sequences of peer blank-line insertions and deletions above, inside and below the claimed block, plus holder edits inside it. Assert the mapped range always equals the holder's actual lines (oracle from the generator), the pushed output never duplicates or loses a line outside withdrawn hunks, and an edit inside the claimed lines is always denied.

findings.title: Decorator, attribute and comment ownership and the key conventions are unpinned: decorator-only edits escape claims, and peers with different conventions splice each other into duplicated decorators
findings.scenario: H holds handler#1, a function with `@app.route("/orders/<id>")` and `@lru_cache` decorators. (a) The extent follows Python ast (`lineno` = the def line, which the research suggests for exact signatures) or tree-sitter's bare function_definition. B changes only the route decorator. (b) One peer computes extents from decorated_definition (tree-sitter), another from the bare def (ast), and the gate splices across them. (c) Peers on different plugin versions use different ordinal conventions ('#1 always' vs 'plain for unique, #2 for duplicates'), grammar versions or queries.
findings.consequence: (a) The decorator edit maps to `<gap after=helper_after_routes>`, so the claim is bypassed. Changing a route is exactly the interface change claims exist to protect. (b) TIP decorated into OUT bare: `@app.route` appears twice (the route registers twice) and `@lru_cache` stacks. The reverse direction deletes both decorators. Both parse cleanly. (c) Every key differs between the two peers, so no claim ever matches: a universal bypass that looks healthy. Leading comments above a def and column-0 comments are owned by no symbol.
findings.evidence_detail: results_all.json S5_decorators_comments: gate_bare.conflict_detected=false (hunk -> '<gap after=f:def:helper_after_routes#1>'), gate_decorated.conflict_detected=true; splice_TIP_decorated_into_OUT_bare route_decorators=2, extra lines '@app.route("/orders/<int:id>")','@lru_cache(maxsize=128)', parses_clean=true; splice_TIP_bare_into_OUT_decorated missing both decorators; ownership map (docstring and body-indented trailing comment -> handler; leading and column-0 comments -> gap). Part (c) is REASONED; the research text implies 'plain for unique' while this harness used '#1 always'.
findings.mitigation: Rules: (1) Region extent = decorated_definition / attribute_list-inclusive node plus directly attached leading comments (no blank line between them), produced by ONE parser (the pinned tree-sitter WASM). Python ast may classify signatures but never supplies ranges. (2) A regionSpec id is published per peer on the board: sha256 of each grammar .wasm, query file hash, extent convention, ordinal convention, plugin version. Claims carry the regionSpec they were computed with. Between peers with different regionSpecs, all claims degrade to whole-file. (3) Because claims are line ranges, cross-peer matching does not depend on names at all; the regionSpec only governs how the holder chooses its own ranges.
findings.test: Decorator-only edit fixture: assert it is denied while handler is held. Run two simulated daemons with different extent conventions or grammar hashes: assert the board shows the mismatch, claims become whole-file between them, and no pushed blob gains or loses a decorator line.

findings.title: A claim published under the old name does not cover the renamed symbol when code and board arrive out of step
findings.scenario: The holder's Edit renames compute_total to compute_sum and edits its body. The alias compute_total->compute_sum is computed in PostToolUse. Before PostToolUse runs, the debounced snapshot (the file fence blocks daemon writes, not snapshots) or a non-atomic host pushes the rename on the code ref while the board still says compute_total. A reader's two-refspec fetch can also see a new code ref with an old board. The requester's daemon merges, and B's in-window edit lands cleanly in compute_sum.
findings.consequence: The gate maps B's hunk to compute_sum#1. The only published claim is compute_total#1, which resolves to nothing in OUT ('key missing in OUT'), so B's change to the claimed function is pushed (conflict_detected=false). With the alias applied, the same gate withdraws it byte-correctly, so the bypass exists purely from timing.
findings.evidence_detail: results_all.json S1_rename_in_window: merge_conflicts=0, gate_with_claim_under_old_name_only {conflict_detected:false, splice_note:'key missing in OUT', pushes_requester_change:true}; gate_with_alias_applied byte_equal=true; line_tracked byte_equal=true. The orderings (snapshot before PostToolUse, --atomic unsupported, non-atomic multi-ref fetch) are REASONED from decisions 2/5.
findings.mitigation: Rules: (1) A claim record carries claimCommit, the code OID its ranges refer to. The gate uses a claim only after mapping its ranges forward from claimCommit to TIP. If claimCommit is not an ancestor of TIP (board ahead of code), the claim's path is held whole-file this round. If TIP contains newer holder commits than the claim, the forward map still applies. (2) A fenced file is excluded from snapshots, not just from daemon writes, until its PostToolUse has republished the claim ranges. (3) A missing key is never read as 'no conflict'. With line tracking there is no key lookup to miss.
findings.test: Simulate: the holder renames and pushes code without the board update (inject a board lag); the requester edits the renamed body. Assert the requester's hunk is withdrawn or queued, never pushed. Repeat with the board ahead of the code (claimCommit not yet fetched) and assert whole-file hold for that path.

findings.title: 'Rename = re-resolve by edit offset, then publish alias' fires when an Edit inserts a new def at the claimed function's start
findings.scenario:
The holder's Edit uses old_string='def parse(value):' and new_string='def parse_v2(value): ...


def parse(value):'. A common pattern when adding a wrapper or variant. PostToolUse re-resolves the claim at the edit's start offset in the new tree.
findings.consequence: The key at that offset is now parse_v2#1, so the daemon publishes alias parse->parse_v2 although parse still exists (lines 5346-5350). The claim moves to the new wrapper and the original function is unprotected. The interface-change detector broadcasts 'parse removed/renamed' to every Claude, which may then 'fix' callers of a function that was never renamed. Under the push governor this is costly noise, and the behaviour is wrong.
findings.evidence_detail: extra_results.json false_alias: claim_key_at_PreToolUse='f:def:parse#1', key_at_same_offset_after_edit='f:def:parse_v2#1', old_key_still_resolves_after=true; genuine rename for comparison: old key no longer resolves.
findings.mitigation: Rule: claims follow lines, not offsets. PostToolUse computes the exact line delta from old_string/new_string at the matched line, so the claimed range keeps covering the original function's lines and the inserted lines become a new claim. A name alias is published, for display and interface-change notices only, when all three hold: the old qualname no longer resolves in the post-edit tree, the new qualname did not exist pre-edit, and at least 60% of body lines match.
findings.test: Fixtures: insert a def before the claimed one at the same offset; genuine rename; rename plus body rewrite. Assert alias and 'removed' notices fire only for the genuine renames, and the original function stays claimed in the insert case.

findings.title: One half-typed line in a pushed snapshot (autosave, or a Claude mid-way through a multi-step edit) wipes out or scrambles the symbol keys of hundreds of functions on every peer
findings.scenario: An editor autosaves, or a Write lands, an unclosed construct in func_0100 (line ~1,427 of the 5,958-line file). It is snapshotted and pushed, so every peer's tree is now broken. Each daemon re-resolves claims and maps hunks on that tree.
findings.consequence: Unclosed `"""`: an ERROR node spans lines 1-5,962; keys drop from 437 to 106; every claim below the break (compute_total, parse, handler, Account) resolves to nothing, so edits there pass ungated (they map to `<toplevel after=const:msg>`). Unclosed `(`: functions func_0101..func_0379 (279 functions, about 3,600 lines) vanish into an ERROR and 282 spurious const:total#n keys appear. An edit inside func_0150 maps to `<toplevel after=const:total>#50`, a garbage key that can collide with real claims (false block) or be published as a claim. JS unclosed `{` in render: 13 keys become 3. C# unclosed `{` in Calc(int): 7 keys become 0. The trees are deterministic: incremental reparse (keystroke by keystroke) and cold parse give identical node ranges, so every peer agrees on the broken keys.
findings.evidence_detail: results_all.json S7_error_nodes (py_unclosed_triple_quote_in_func_0100 n_keys_broken=106, errors [ERROR,1,5962], watched all null; py_unclosed_paren_in_func_0100 n_keys_broken=717, n_func_keys_broken=141; js_unclosed_brace_in_render keys_broken has 3 entries; cs_unclosed_brace_in_Calc_int keys_broken=[]). Spot check: edit in func_0150 -> 'f:toplevel:<toplevel after=const:total>#50'. fwd_results.json incremental_vs_cold: same_node_ranges=true for 3 cases (17-26 keystrokes). That last part is a negative result.
findings.mitigation: Rules: (1) Never derive or re-resolve claim ranges from a tree with ERROR or MISSING nodes. Claims keep their last-good ranges and are carried forward by line diff, which needs no parse. (2) If a local hunk falls inside an ERROR span at LAST_APPLIED or at OUT, treat it as touching every claim in that file (whole-file conflict) until a clean tree is seen. (3) Never publish a new claim key computed from an erroring tree; the holder claims the whole file instead. (4) Never compute keys on a blob containing conflict markers.
findings.test: Use the S7 fixtures as pushed TIP states. Assert all existing claims still deny edits to their (mapped) lines, no claim is published with a key from the broken tree, and a requester's edit anywhere in the broken file is held while any claim exists in it. Clear the error and assert normal symbol-level behaviour resumes.

findings.title: If the 'published symbol text' is taken from the board (captured at claim time) instead of from the exact TIP being leased, the splice reverts the holder's own later edits
findings.scenario: The holder claims K at t0 and the board records K's text T0. The holder keeps editing K, and TIP now holds T2. Requester B's gate withdraws B's in-window change to K by splicing in 'the published symbol text', read from the board, or from a TIP fetched before the last CAS retry.
findings.consequence: The pushed commit sets K back to T0, wiping out the holder's T1/T2 edits. The commit is attributed to B, every peer applies it, and the holder's working tree is reverted by the next merge. After a CAS reject and refetch, a splice built against the previous TIP has the same effect.
findings.evidence_detail: Follows from the splice definition in decision 2/approved gate design. The pipeline in this harness always took the source from the TIP OID being merged, which is why S1/S3/S6 'with alias'/line-tracked cases were byte-correct.
findings.mitigation: Rules: there is no splice source text at all. Withdrawal removes local hunks from SNAPSHOT before the merge, and the merge takes TIP's text. The board stores ranges and hashes only, never code. Every gate computation is keyed to the exact TIP OID used as the --force-with-lease value; a CAS reject invalidates it, and the gate is recomputed from scratch on the new TIP.
findings.test: The holder makes 3 successive pushes to K while the requester's gate is forced to retry CAS twice. Assert the final pushed K equals the holder's latest version byte for byte, and assert (static check) that no board record field contains source text.

findings.title: Corrupt splices parse cleanly, so 'tree-sitter has no errors' cannot catch duplicated or lost code; a hunk-subset tripwire can
findings.scenario: Any gate implementation that validates its output by re-parsing (has_error == false) before pushing.
findings.consequence: Parsing passed every corruption in this sweep: duplicate functions (S2, S3), duplicate setter (S3 JS), deleted claimed lines (S4), reverted unclaimed change (S6 span), duplicate overload (S6 pairwise), wrong sub-block (S9), duplicated decorators (S5), and even invalid UTF-8 (S8). Python and JS accept redefinition. C# CS0111 only surfaces at compile time.
findings.evidence_detail: parses_clean=true in every corrupt verdict in results_all.json. guard_results.json: invariant G6 (each hunk of diff(TIP,output) is an exact hunk of diff(TIP,OUT)) plus G7 (each withdrawn hunk overlaps a foreign claim's TIP lines) flagged all 8 corrupt splices and passed the 5 correct ones. Two false positives (S10, where git merges a withdrawn hunk with an adjacent kept hunk) lead to a conservative hold, not corruption. Negative results: node-range splices with an adjacent added or deleted symbol (S10a/b) were byte-correct, and diff-slider attribution was clean under git default, --no-indent-heuristic, minimal, patience and difflib for JS, C# and Python same-tail insertions (extra_results.json slider_negative).
findings.mitigation: Rule: before any push, per changed path: output must be valid UTF-8; diff(TIP,output) hunks must be a subset of diff(TIP,OUT) hunks; every withdrawn hunk must overlap a foreign claim range or be a group-name insertion; the ERROR-node count must not exceed max(TIP, OUT); no (path, kind, qualname) count may exceed max(TIP, OUT). On any violation, hold that path (push the others), queue the whole-file diff, and surface it in /cowork status. Never 'repair' and push.
findings.test: Run every corrupting fixture from this sweep (S2, S3x3, S4, S5x2, S6x2, S8, S9) through the real gate with the tripwire. Assert zero pushes of the affected path and a queued item for each. Run the correct fixtures (S1, S6 remove, S7, S10, forward-map variants) and assert they push byte-identical to the oracle.

design_changes: Replace name-keyed claim matching and 'splice published symbol text into the outgoing blob' with LINE-TRACKED claims. Claim = {path, claimCommit (code OID the ranges refer to, pushed with or before the claim), stored-form 1-based line ranges (one per member for groups), label key path+kind+qualname (display only), regionSpec id}. The holder republishes ranges on every push. Peers map ranges forward with `git diff -U0 claimCommit TIP`. VERIFIED: correct in 4/4 variants (22-line insertion far above, directly above, directly after, after-with-same-tail; fwd_results.json). It fixed S1, S3 (py, js), S4, S6a and S9 byte for byte (results_all.json line_tracked entries). Reason: every name-derived key component (#n, after=X, overload-group spans, block ordinals) changes when anyone edits outside the symbol, and those keys silently corrupted or bypassed in 9 harness scenarios.

Gate order: withdraw BEFORE the merge, verify AFTER it. (1) Map foreign claim ranges into LAST_APPLIED coordinates; if claimCommit has no ancestry relation with LAST_APPLIED, hold the whole file. (2) Remove the local hunks of diff(LAST_APPLIED, SNAPSHOT) that overlap a claim (insertions count only strictly inside; for group claims, also insertions declaring a member with the group's name) into the queue, giving SNAPSHOT'. (3) OUT = merge-tree(LAST_APPLIED, SNAPSHOT', TIP). A conflicted path is held whole-file and its hunks queued; no -X/--union/--ours. (4) Identity check: each kept local hunk must sit in the same locally computed symbol in SNAPSHOT and OUT. (5) Tripwire: UTF-8 valid, diff(TIP,OUT) a subset of the expected hunks, no added ERROR nodes, no qualname count increase. Any failure holds that path and pushes the rest. Reason: git merge-tree itself moved a requester's edit into a neighbouring same-tail function with exit 0 (VERIFIED), which no post-merge region check can attribute back. Pre-merge withdrawal was byte-correct (premerge_results.json).

Why the suggested rule 'splice only when the region's base text hash matches on both sides' is insufficient. If 'base' means the common ancestor, both peers resolve parse#1 to the same base text in S3 (the stubs are new, the function is unchanged), so the hashes match, the splice proceeds and duplicates the holder's function. If it means 'OUT region vs base region', a mismatch cannot distinguish 'requester legitimately edited K (withdraw it)' from 'key now points at a different symbol' (S3, S4, S9). The rule therefore either blocks every legitimate withdrawal or lets misidentified ones through. Line tracking supplies the missing distinction; a hash may only serve as a post-mapping verification field.

All cross-component coordinates are (stored-form blob OID, line numbers). The daemon parses the stored blob (git cat-file) and reads only startPosition.row and endPosition.row. These are identical across py-tree-sitter and web-tree-sitter and across BOM/CRLF forms (VERIFIED, 435/9/8 nodes). startIndex/endIndex are UTF-16 code units in web-tree-sitter and must never be used as byte offsets. The PreToolUse deny-at-edit path uses the same mapping (old_string -> line in the current file -> LAST_APPLIED -> claim ranges), so edit-time and push-time decisions agree.

Publish a regionSpec per peer on the board: grammar .wasm sha256, query hash, extent convention (decorated_definition / attribute-inclusive plus attached comments), ordinal convention, plugin version. Between peers whose regionSpec differs, every claim degrades to whole-file. Python ast may classify signatures but never supply ranges.

Aliases (rename/move) become display and interface-notice metadata only, published under strict conditions (old qualname gone, new qualname new, at least 60% body-line overlap). Claim continuity comes from line tracking through the holder's own edits, using the exact delta of old_string/new_string.

Paths with a filter= attribute, and blobs containing conflict markers or ERROR nodes, get no region-level withdrawal: whole-file hold only. Text from the working tree never enters a blob except via the private-index `git add` or `hash-object --path`.
open_questions: web-tree-sitter 0.27: is there a supported way to parse UTF-8 bytes so indices are byte offsets? The design above avoids needing it (rows only), but if any component already relies on startIndex, it must be found and removed.

Over-withdrawal policy: git merges a withdrawn hunk with an adjacent legitimate hunk (S10), so the gate either holds a correct file (G6 false positive) or queues the requester's adjacent addition along with the claimed change. Which behaviour is acceptable to the user: hold the file, or push without the adjacent addition and queue it?

The same-tail merge misplacement also happens with no claims at all (pure 3-way merge identity loss). Should the post-merge identity check hold unclaimed files too, or only files containing a foreign claim? This overlaps the distributed-protocol and merge lens.
C# partial-type enumeration across files: is a repo-wide `git grep` index per TIP acceptable for latency, or should group claims on partial types always be whole-type, meaning every partial file?

When claimCommit is unrelated to LAST_APPLIED (after 'save' resets the live ref onto a new branch commit), should claims be re-based by the holder (republished against the new root) before anyone can be gated by them? Until then this design falls back to whole-file holds.

Severity calibration for the real 1.3 MB hub.py was not measured (the real repo was not touched). Its Hangul density and line count (26,436) mean drift numbers will be much larger than the fixture's, and an unclosed construct near the top would likely wipe out thousands of keys.

gapResults.lens: gap:Lifecycle of held, quarantined, pinned and parked local hunks (interaction between revert guards, the push gate, the conflict policy and claims)

findings.title: A held revert of a peer's change is published when the local Claude claims the same symbol for an unrelated edit
findings.scenario: 1) B's Claude claims foo(), changes `y = x + 1` to `y = x + 2  # fix`, publishes, finishes; B's claim is released. 2) A's daemon applies it. 3) A's human saves a stale editor buffer of f.py, so line 6 is `x + 1` again. The per-line revert detector blames line 6 to B, so the hunk goes into the contested set and is held. 4) A's Claude is asked to change foo(). PreToolUse(Edit) maps the edit to foo, sees no published claim and takes a local claim. The edit changes `return w * 2`, 3 lines below the held line. 5) Next loop: the contested-set rule 'exempt if a local session holds a claim on that symbol' drops the hold. The same thing happens inside the propagation window: if A's local claim races B's still-unseen claim, the code leaves in the same atomic push as the claim, before board order can mark A as the conflict causer.
findings.consequence: A's push contains `y = x + 1` plus Claude's line. B's daemon applies it, so B's fix disappears from the live ref and from B's disk. No warning is raised: the board shows a legitimate claim, the detector was suppressed, and A's disk minus LA is now empty, so the hold is simply gone. Claude's unrelated claim has laundered a human's accidental revert.
findings.evidence_detail: sweep/hold/exp_a.py (real merge-tree/commit-tree/push --force-with-lease on a file:// bare remote; def-scan symbol map; detector = `git blame --porcelain` on the live chain). Variant claim_exempts gives 'live foo(): y = x + 1 ... return int(w * 2)', 'B disk line 6: y = x + 1'. The fixed variant (claims ignored, merge-mask with H0/H1) keeps live = B fix + int(); A disk minus LA = exactly '-y = x + 2 # B fix / +y = x + 1'. The exemption rule is my reconstruction of the human-git-lifecycle contested-set rule, as quoted in the gap brief.
findings.mitigation: Rule H1: claim state is never an input to the hold or mask functions. A claim cannot exempt, release, narrow or re-key a hold. Rule H2: taint is per line. A hunk is revert-tainted if it deletes or modifies any line whose live provenance is another author, whatever else the hunk adds. Only the tainted lines are masked (see merge-mask). Rule H3: a held region also blocks the local Claude. PreToolUse(Edit/MultiEdit/Write) denies any edit whose old_string range, or whose Write diff, overlaps a held region within ±1 line. The denial names the hold id, the peer and `/cowork hold show <id>`. Rule H4: a revert hold leaves the ACTIVE state only through an explicit human `/cowork resolve <id> --publish|--discard|--park` or the automatic SUBSUMED transition (the team itself already has the change).
findings.test: Replay exp_a against the real daemon. After the Claude Edit, the live tip must contain both B's line and Claude's line. A's `diff(LA, disk)` must equal the held hunk byte-for-byte. The board must list hold <id> as ACTIVE with an age. Race variant: deliver B's claim to A only after A's local claim; assert the same three facts. Property test: interleave claims, releases and stale-buffer saves at random; assert no pushed commit deletes or modifies a line blamed to another peer unless a resolve --publish event for that hold id exists.

findings.title: A hold keyed by line range misses after a peer inserts lines above it, publishes the revert and overwrites the peer's lines
findings.scenario: A holds the revert at f.py line 6, stored as (path, start=6, n=1, original lines), and masks by replacing lines 6..6 of the outgoing blob with the stored original. C inserts 40 constant lines under `import os` and publishes. A's sync 3-way-merges them (clean), so the held line moves to 46 on A's disk. Later, A's Claude edits g.py, which triggers a publish. Detection is incremental and the hold is pinned (acknowledged 'keep local'), so the detector does not re-derive it.
findings.consequence: Two silent corruptions in one push. First, line 6 of the outgoing blob, now C's `C_CONST_03 = 3`, is replaced with `    y = x + 2  # B fix`. That leaves an indented stray line at module level (IndentationError) and C's constant is lost. Second, foo() at line 46 ships `y = x + 1`, so B's fix is reverted on live and on B's disk.
findings.evidence_detail: sweep/hold/exp_bc.py b1/linerange: 'live foo() first body line: y = x + 1', 'module-level indented lines before foo: [(6, y = x + 2 # B fix)]', 'C's inserted lines missing: [C_CONST_03]'. b1/merge (blob-pair + merge-file mask): live keeps B fix; A's disk diff shows the hold rebased to line 46.
findings.mitigation: Rule H5: holds have no positional identity. Each hold is stored as a blob pair (H0 = team version of the path when the hold was made, H1 = local version) in a commit under refs/cowork-local/<b>/holds, mirrored to the board. The outgoing blob is computed as `git merge-file -p --object-id <S_disk blob> <H1'> <H0'>`, a revert-by-merge. Line numbers are recomputed from that merge for display only. Rule H6: after every successful apply, rebase each hold: H0' = new LA blob, H1' = merge-file(cur=H0', base=H0, other=H1); see stale-hold-resurrects-team-revert.
findings.test: Property test over random peer ops: insert or delete 1-40 lines above or below, modify far lines, delete far lines. A has one held line and one unrelated local edit. Assert the published blob == team tip + A's non-held edit exactly (computed independently by merge-file). Zero mismatches are allowed. exp_j_fuzz.py already passes 160/160 with the rebased operator.

findings.title: A hold keyed by hunk identity (patch-id, or pre/post-image hashes plus base blob oid) stops matching after a nearby local edit or an incoming change in its context
findings.scenario: (b2) A's hold is keyed by `git patch-id --stable` of the -U3 hunk. A's Claude edits line 8 (`w = z - 4` to `w = z - 5`), 2 lines below the held line 6. `git diff` now yields one hunk containing both changes, and its patch-id differs from the stored one. (c1) Instead, C edits line 8 and publishes. A's sync merges it cleanly, so the held hunk's context lines change and its patch-id differs again. The key proposed in the gap brief, (path, base blob oid, pre-image hash, post-image hash), breaks the same way: the base blob oid changes at every peer apply to the file, and pre/post-image hashes change as soon as hunks merge or context shifts.
findings.consequence: The mask matches 0 hunks, so the held revert ships together with the legitimate change. In b2, live gets `y = x + 1` plus `w = z - 5`. In c1, live gets `y = x + 1` plus C's annotation. B's fix is reverted on every peer, and A's registry still lists the hold as active, so `/cowork status` claims it is safe.
findings.evidence_detail: sweep/hold/exp_bc.py: b2/patchid prints 'patch-id mask: 1 hunk(s), 0 matched hold' then 'RESULT: B FIX REVERTED IN foo ON LIVE'. c1/patchid prints the same. With the merge-mask both give 'B fix survives'.
findings.mitigation: Use content keys (path + H0/H1 oids + a pre/post hash) only for dedup and display, never to decide what is masked. What is masked is always the output of the rebased 3-way operator (rule H5/H6), so whether a hold is present is answered by computing, not by matching. Rule H7: on every loop, assert merge-mask(S_disk, holds) == S_pub, and that diff(LA, S_pub) contains no line tainted by any ACTIVE hold. If the assertion fails, stop publishing and raise a doctor error. Never fall back to the unmasked tree.
findings.test: Unit: hold, then a local edit 0, 1, 2 and 3 lines away; then an incoming edit at the same distances. For distance ≥1 assert the masked publish equals team + non-held edit. For distance 0 (adjacent), assert state CONFLICTED and that nothing from that file is published. Integration: kill switch. Corrupt the registry key and assert the daemon refuses to push rather than pushing S_disk.

findings.title: After a clean 3-way merge absorbs an incoming change into the held region, 'region equals an older version' detectors no longer see a revert, and a writer that records the merged blob as applied hides the hold entirely
findings.scenario: A holds the revert at line 6. C changes line 8 of foo() and A's sync merges it: foo() on A's disk = revert + C's line, a text that never existed in history. (i) A detector of the form 'symbol text equals that symbol in an ancestor of LA' returns False. (ii) Suppose the verifying writer (editor-fs lens) or the apply step records what it wrote (M_disk) as the applied base, the private-index seed or LA. Then diff(LA, disk) is empty: the revert is invisible to the detector, the mask and status, and A silently diverges. When the daemon restarts or rejoins, LA is reseeded from the live tip and the revert reappears as an unflagged local change. If that happens after a save (see save-squash-erases-provenance) or outside the blame window, it is published.
findings.consequence: Detection depends on which detector was built. A history-equality detector passes the blended revert, and an absorbed-into-LA implementation hides it until a restart publishes it days later, with no hold id, no board record and no warning.
findings.evidence_detail: sweep/hold/exp_bc.py c1: 'detector[symbol-equals-ancestor] flags foo: False' while 'detector[per-line blame]: [{... authors: [B]}]'. Part (ii), the LA := M_disk variant, is REASONED from merge semantics: merge(base=M_disk, ours=disk, theirs=TIP) returns TIP for that region, so the revert is never pushed but persists on disk unrecorded.
findings.mitigation: Rule H8: LA is only ever a commit fetched from the remote live ref or saved branch, never a locally merged or written tree. The writer may verify against its expected bytes but records nothing as 'applied' except the fetched commit. Rule H9: revert detection is per line (`git blame` over the live chain plus save attribution; see save-squash-erases-provenance). It is never 'region equals history' or 'hunk equals reverse of a peer patch'. Rule H10: each loop checks INV-MASK, disk == LA ⊕ ACTIVE holds ⊕ unpublished local edits, and any residue not accounted for becomes a new hold (state DETECTED) rather than being dropped.
findings.test: Run c1 with each detector implementation behind one interface. The test fails unless the detector flags the blended hunk. Restart test: create a hold, absorb an incoming change, kill -9 the daemon, start it, and assert the hold is re-attached from the registry ref before the first publish and that the live ref is unchanged.

findings.title: A re-mask that is not rebased resurrects a change the team deliberately reverted
findings.scenario: A holds a stale-buffer revert of B's fix (H0 = with fix, H1 = without). Meanwhile the team decides B's fix was wrong, and C's Claude reverts it with B's consent and publishes. A's sync merges cleanly: both sides made the same change, so A's disk now equals the team. The gap brief's rule 'held regions are re-masked from every outgoing tree until resolved by a human command' still applies the original (H0, H1) revert-mask on A's next publish.
findings.consequence: The mask turns `x + 1` back into `x + 2  # B fix` in A's outgoing tree, and the next unrelated push from A re-introduces the fix the team just removed. Every peer, B and C included, receives it. To them it looks as if A's PC reverted C's revert, with no claim and no event. The rule meant to prevent reverts produces one.
findings.evidence_detail: sweep/hold/exp_j_fuzz.py: 160 random trials using real `git merge-file --object-id`. Static (never rebased) mask WRONG in 19/19 'team reverts B fix' trials ('team tip line k = line_10 = 10 | static-masked publish line k = line_10 = 10 + 1  # B fix'). Rebased mask OK 160/160, including 19 SUBSUMED. Same-line peer edits produced a disk-sync conflict 16/16.
findings.mitigation: Rule H6 (rebase after every apply): H0' = LA blob; H1' = merge-file(cur=H0', base=H0, other=H1). If H1' == H0', the hold is SUBSUMED: auto-close it, post one board event 'your held change is now the team version', and tell A's human or Claude. If the merge conflicts, the hold is CONFLICTED: withhold the whole path from publishing, escalate, and stop masking with stale blobs. Masking always uses (H0', H1'), never the originals.
findings.test: exp_j_fuzz as a CI property test (≥1,000 seeded trials, plus shrinking). The invariant is published == T2 + non-held local edit. A dedicated case covers op revert_k (the team makes the identical change): the hold must become SUBSUMED and A must publish nothing for that path.

findings.title: Using the masked (published) tree as the apply BASE makes every incoming change to a held file fail 'not uptodate', and the all-or-nothing apply then blocks all incoming changes
findings.scenario: An implementer keeps one snapshot tree per loop and, to 'honour holds', builds it masked: S_pub, which differs from disk in the held file. The apply runs `read-tree S_pub` into a temp index, `update-index --refresh`, then `read-tree -m -u S_pub M`. C changes bar() in the held file f.py and also changes g.py.
findings.consequence: read-tree exits 128 with "Entry 'f.py' not uptodate. Cannot merge." and writes nothing: g.py stays old too. The retry loop re-snapshots, gets the same masked tree and fails again. A receives no more changes from anyone while the hold lives (it can live for days), but A's own pushes are still accepted, so peers see A as healthy.
findings.evidence_detail: sweep/hold/exp_more.py d1: 'BASE=S_pub: read-tree -m -u exit 128 | error: Entry 'f.py' not uptodate. Cannot merge.' and 'g.py on disk after failed apply: return 0'. With BASE=S_disk (stat-valid add -A index), the same incoming change applies, g.py = 42, bar updated, and the held line stays on disk.
findings.mitigation: Rule H11 (two trees per loop): S_disk (the add -A result, stat-valid) is the only BASE for merge-tree and read-tree -m -u. S_pub = mask(S_disk, holds) is used only for the outgoing merge-tree(LA, S_pub, TIP) and the push. Holds never change what is written to disk except through their own explicit transitions (park, resolve). Rule H12: N consecutive apply failures (default 3) for the same reason is a health state published to the board ('A not receiving since 10:02'), not a silent retry.
findings.test: Integration: create a hold on f.py, have a peer change f.py elsewhere and also g.py, and assert both arrive on A's disk within 2 loops. Assert the board health record of A shows receiving=ok. Negative test: inject the masked-base bug and assert the health watchdog posts 'not receiving' within N loops.

findings.title: A save collapses the live chain into one commit by the saver, so a stale-buffer revert right after the save no longer looks like a revert of a peer
findings.scenario: B fixes foo() at 10:00 and it propagates. At 10:01 A runs `/cowork save`: one commit on main by A with the live tree (per-symbol attribution only as trailers), then the live ref is reset onto that commit. At 10:02 A's editor, which loaded f.py before 10:00, autosaves or the human hits Ctrl+S.
findings.consequence: `git blame` on the new live chain attributes line 6 to A, so the per-line detector returns no taint and no hold is made. A's daemon publishes `x + 1` and B's fix is reverted everywhere. This is the most common moment for stale buffers, because saves happen at natural pauses when people switch files. Any holds whose provenance is recomputed after the save lose their 'peer' attribution in the same way.
findings.evidence_detail: sweep/hold/exp_more.py h: blame line 6 before save 'author B', after save ['author A']; per-line provenance detector after the stale save = [] (not flagged). The squash-save shape is my assumption of decision 10's save ('commits the shared tree … with per-symbol attribution').
findings.mitigation: Rule H13: provenance survives saves. Either (a) save writes one commit per contributing author (author = that peer, tree = cumulative), so blame keeps working; or (b) the daemon keeps a provenance map (path, line-hash) -> (author, live commit, time) in the board ref that is not reset at save, and the detector consults it with a time window (e.g. 24 h) that spans saves. Rule H14: holds are rebased onto the save commit like any apply (tree-identical, so a no-op), and they keep their original authors and peers in registry metadata, not in recomputed blame. Rule H14b: save commits the tree of the fetched live-tip commit after a final sync round, never S_disk or S_pub from the saver's PC. The saver's ACTIVE holds are listed in the save report and stay ACTIVE, rebased onto C.
findings.test: Replay h against the real daemon. After the save, a stale save of the pre-fix file must create a revert hold naming B, and the live ref must be unchanged. Repeat with 3 authors in one save and assert that each line's provenance is the original author.

findings.title: After the save-time branch/index move, held hunks look like ordinary uncommitted changes and leave through a normal `git commit && git push`, outside every cowork gate
findings.scenario: The git-integrity lens proposes moving each peer's branch ref and index to the save commit C (`reset --mixed` equivalent). A has an ACTIVE revert hold on foo(). `git status` on A now shows f.py as modified relative to C, and the human believes that is their own work. They run `git commit -am wip && git push`, or A's Claude runs it through Bash for an unrelated task. The real branch moves, so cowork performs its live 'rebase' onto the new branch head.
findings.consequence: The revert is now in a branch commit. When the live session rebases onto the moved branch it treats the commit as authoritative, every peer applies it, and B's fix is gone. The hold registry still says 'held', so status contradicts reality. The same path leaks a hold created because the clean filter failed (a plaintext secret) straight into branch history.
findings.evidence_detail: Combines the git-integrity design change (post-save index/branch move) with hold-on-disk semantics. The leak path itself is plain git: committed working-tree changes go to the branch regardless of the cowork registry. Not reproduced end to end because the live-rebase-on-branch-move rule is not yet specified.
findings.mitigation: Rule H15: when the real branch moves for a reason other than a cowork save, run the hold registry and the per-line revert detector over diff(old base, new branch head) before rebasing live. Any branch hunk equal to an ACTIVE or PARKED hold (tested by rebasing the hold onto it and getting SUBSUMED), or tainted against peer provenance, pauses the live rebase for that path and posts a team event naming the commit. Rule H16: PreToolUse(Bash) matching `git commit`, `git stash` or `git push` while ACTIVE holds exist on staged paths returns a deny with the hold list; humans see the hold list in `/cowork status` and in the statusline. Optionally, `/cowork doctor` offers a pre-commit hook; it is never installed silently.
findings.test: Integration: create an ACTIVE hold, perform a human `git commit -am` and push to main, and assert that the live ref does not take the revert, that a board event names the commit, and that A's hold moves to CONFLICTED(branch). For the Claude path, issue a Bash `git commit -am` through the hook harness and assert the deny JSON lists the hold.

findings.title: Parked or held state stored under refs/worktree/* (or any unlogged local ref) is deleted with the worktree, has no reflog when overwritten, and is pruned by gc
findings.scenario: human-git-lifecycle parks join- or stop-time work in refs/worktree/cowork/<b>/parked and restores the files to the team version. Because the park is off disk, `git status` in that worktree is empty. (1) The user, or Claude Code's own exit cleanup, removes the worktree: unnamed `--worktree` sessions and subagent worktrees are auto-removed when clean. (2) Alternatively, a second park (join, then later `stop --park`) writes the same ref name. (3) The user's `git gc` runs later.
findings.consequence: (1) `git worktree remove` exits 0 without a prompt, and the park ref disappears. (2) The first park is overwritten, and refs/worktree/* and refs/cowork-local/* have no reflog by default, so it cannot be recovered. (3) gc --prune=now (or the 2-week default) deletes the objects. The parked human work is gone with no message, which breaks 'nothing is ever lost'.
findings.evidence_detail: sweep/hold/exp_more.py e: 'worktree status before remove: ""', 'git worktree remove exit 0', no ref mentioning 'parked' afterwards, 'park#1 object exists after gc --prune=now: False'; `git reflog show` for both namespaces is empty after an overwrite. Docs: core.logAllRefUpdates=true auto-creates reflogs only for refs/heads, refs/remotes, refs/notes and HEAD (local git-config.html, 2.55). Claude Code removes a clean worktree automatically for unnamed sessions and when a subagent finishes without changes (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/worktrees, 'Clean up worktrees').
findings.mitigation: Rule H17: every hold, park, quarantine and conflict blob lives in one append-only registry. It is a commit chain under the common refs namespace (refs/cowork-local/<b>/holds, shared by all worktrees), and each update is a new commit whose parent is the previous registry commit, so nothing is overwritten. Write it with `update-ref --create-reflog` as a second net. Never use refs/worktree/* for durable state. Rule H18: within one loop (≤ 3 s), mirror each registry commit to the board ref so the objects are reachable from the remote (see local-only-holds-break-nothing-lost). Rule H19: the daemon registers a WorktreeRemove/SessionEnd hook warning, and `/cowork status` counts parked items per worktree. Candidate, not yet a rule (see open questions): report a worktree with PARKED items as 'not clean' to Claude Code's cleanup through an untracked marker file.
findings.test: Integration: park in a linked worktree, remove the worktree, run gc --prune=now, and assert the park is still listed by `/cowork holds` and restorable. Park twice under the same session and assert both parks are listed. Re-clone test: fresh clone + `/cowork start` lists both parks from the board.

findings.title: Holds that exist only on one PC are lost by re-clone, `uninstall --purge`, `stop` or disk loss, and mirroring them naively leaks secrets and burns push budget
findings.scenario: Seven proposed stores (refs/cowork-held/*, refs/worktree/…/parked*, .git/cowork/quarantine/*.patch, .git/cowork/conflicts/*, refs/cowork-local/…/conflicts/*, board records, a 14-day write ring) are mostly local. A has a conflict stage-2 blob and a quarantined patch (the published version is on disk), and a pending handoff that has not been pushed yet. A's human runs `/cowork uninstall --purge` to fix a broken install, or re-clones the repo, or the laptop dies. A second case: the obvious fix, 'mirror every hold to the board', also mirrors a hold that exists because the clean filter failed (the plaintext secret is the held content), and writes a hold record with a timestamp every loop.
findings.consequence: Case 1: A's displaced work (not on disk, not on live) is deleted, contradicting decision 7. Case 2: the board ref carries the secret to every clone and to GitHub's cruft packs. A hold record rewritten each loop changes the board tree each loop, so a single permanent hold consumes the team's 6 pushes/min.
findings.evidence_detail: Local-only storage follows from the store list in the gap brief. The secret leak path follows from the sibling finding filter-passthrough-leak (sweep/e1: a failing clean filter leaves the raw value in the blob). The budget burn follows from 'push only when the tree changed' (decision 3).
findings.mitigation: Rule H20: a hold is durable only when its registry commit is reachable from the remote board ref. Until then, `/cowork stop`, `uninstall`, `--purge` and `save` refuse with a list. Overrides are `--discard-holds=<ids>` (logged as RESOLVED_DISCARD board events) or `--export <dir>` (writes bundles). Rule H21: holds whose guard set includes filter-failure, secret-scan or 'unreadable' are LOCAL-ONLY by type, never mirrored, and the board gets only a content-free stub (id, path, guard, age). Rule H22: board hold records are content-addressed (id + state + H0'/H1' oids) and change only on state transitions or rebases that change H0'/H1'. Age is computed by readers from created_at, never rewritten. Board pushes are batched with the next code push. Rule H23: `/cowork start` in a fresh clone lists the user's mirrored holds from the board and offers 3-way restore.
findings.test: Integration: create one hold of each kind, run `uninstall --purge`, and assert refusal. Then wait one loop, purge, re-clone, start, and assert every non-secret hold is listed and restorable byte-exact by 3-way merge. Secret test: break the filter, create a filter-failure hold, and assert `git cat-file -p` of every board object never contains the plaintext. Budget test: one permanent hold for 30 minutes with no edits gives 0 pushes after the first.

findings.title: A quarantine stored as a unified .patch and later applied with `git apply` lands cleanly in the wrong function
findings.scenario: The negotiation lens stores A's withdrawn or blocked change as .git/cowork/quarantine/<id>.patch, which changes `process(x)` to `process(x, opts)` in two(). In this codebase two() has the same 3-line context as one(), which is common in C# and JS handlers. Before `/cowork resolve` runs, a peer adds 10 lines at the top of the file, exactly one function's length. The same applies to `stop --park` restores done with `git apply` or `checkout <park-tree> -- path`.
findings.consequence: `git apply` exits 0 with 'Applied patch h.py cleanly' and no offset warning, but the change lands in one(). The wrong function is modified silently, and the resolved state is published as A's deliberate change. A checkout-based restore is worse: it overwrites the whole file with the parked version and reverts every team change since the park.
findings.evidence_detail: sweep/hold/exp_f.py: hunk '@@ -13,7 +13,7 @@ def two(x):' after a +10-line shift gives 'git apply exit 0 | Checking patch h.py... Applied patch h.py cleanly.' and 'landed in: one()  <-- WRONG FUNCTION'. `git merge-file -p --object-id cur H0 H1` with the same data lands in two().
findings.mitigation: Rule H24: no store keeps changes as positional patches or whole-file snapshots meant to be checked out. Every held, parked, quarantined or conflicted change is a blob pair (H0, H1) or a triple (stage 1, stage 2, stage 3) in the registry, plus a .patch rendered for humans only. Rule H25: restore or resolve is always merge-file(cur=current disk blob, base=H0', other=H1') after rebasing. A conflict becomes a visible resolve session with the three versions, never a fuzzy apply and never a checkout.
findings.test: Run the exp_f fixture against the resolve and restore code paths, with shifts of 0, +N and −N lines and identical neighbouring blocks. Assert the change lands in the intended symbol (checked through the tree-sitter symbol map), or that the result is a conflict. Assert that `git apply` is never invoked on a stored hold (code grep in CI).

findings.title: A pending (locked or unreadable) incoming path whose base is advanced to the team tip publishes the stale on-disk bytes as a revert; a blind write at unlock clobbers local edits
findings.scenario: B adds a row to book.csv. On A, Excel has book.csv open, so the per-path tolerant apply skips it, but the daemon sets LA := TIP (the whole commit). A's Claude edits f.py and A publishes. Second variant: the daemon caches B's blob and writes it when the lock clears. Meanwhile A's Claude or human edited the file in place: some editors write in place, which a delete-lock does not block (sweep/e2 shows read-tree failing only at unlink).
findings.consequence: Variant 1: diff(LA, disk) is the reverse of B's change, so A's next push removes B's row from live and from B's disk. The revert detector misses it if it only looks at A-authored hunks, or fires on A's 'human revert' that A never made. Variant 2: A's edits are overwritten by the cached blob with no merge.
findings.evidence_detail:
sweep/hold/exp_more.py g: 'A pushed: True | live book.csv: a,b
1,2
 | B disk: a,b
1,2
' (B's '3,4' row gone). Variant 2 is REASONED.
findings.mitigation: Rule H26: pending is a hold of kind INCOMING with its own per-path base. The private index and LA view for that path stay at the old blob, so diff(LA_path, disk) is zero for unchanged bytes. The outgoing tree uses merge-tree with a per-path base map, or equivalently S_pub takes the TIP blob for that path whenever disk == old blob. Rule H27: release on unlock is a fresh 3-way merge(base=old blob, ours=current disk, theirs=current TIP blob), never a write of the cached blob. Rule H28: pending paths have an age and are listed on the board ('A has not received book.csv for 12 min: locked by EXCEL.EXE').
findings.test: Hold book.csv with FileShare.Read from PowerShell (as in sweep/e2), push a peer change to it and a local edit elsewhere, and assert the live ref keeps the peer's row. Release the lock after a local in-place edit and assert the result contains both the peer row and the local edit.

findings.title: One human change recorded by two guards (revert hold + conflict stage-2, or quarantine + handoff) is resolved twice, or blocks forever as a stale duplicate
findings.scenario: (x1) A holds a revert of B's line, then C edits the same line. A's sync conflicts, and the conflict policy puts C's version on disk and stores stage-2, whose blob oid is identical to the hold's H1, as a new conflict record. The original revert hold now mask-conflicts against a disk that no longer contains it. (i) A blocked change, adding helper(), goes into the holder's queue as a handoff, and also into A's local conflict or quarantine store. B accepts and adds helper() near the end of the file with a tweak. Later A runs `/cowork resolve` on its local copy.
findings.consequence: (x1) A ghost hold stays CONFLICTED, its file is withheld from publishing, and the age counter alarms indefinitely; or the user resolves both records and each one replays the same revert. (i) The 3-way resolve is clean (exit 0) and produces two `def helper` definitions. Python silently uses the later one, and in JS or C# it is a duplicate-member error or a shadowing bug. The holder's adapted version is overridden.
findings.evidence_detail: sweep/hold/exp_bc.py x1: 'conflict record stage2 = cc7e6c0… == hold H1? True' and 'merge-mask CONFLICT (1) -> escalate'. exp_more.py i: 'resolve via 3-way exit 0 | def helper count: 2'.
findings.mitigation: Rule H29: one change has one id. A guard that catches a change already in the registry (same H1 oid, or a pending H1' that rebases onto it) adds itself to that id's guard set instead of creating a record. A conflict on a held path transitions the existing hold to CONFLICTED and stores stage 1/2/3 on it. Rule H30: resolution is a CAS on the id's state in the board ref (ACTIVE→OFFERED→ACCEPTED is one record). Every store or view checks the board state before acting, and resolving an id that is ACCEPTED, RESOLVED or SUBSUMED is a no-op with a message. Rule H31: when a handoff is ACCEPTED, the holder's daemon records the published commit in the id, so the requester's next rebase marks it SUBSUMED. The symbol-level check (helper defined twice) is reported, not auto-merged.
findings.test: Replay x1: assert exactly one registry id exists after the conflict and that its state is CONFLICTED with stages attached. Replay i: B accepts the handoff, then A runs resolve; assert a no-op and that the helper count in the live tree is 1. Property: for every id, the number of RESOLVED_PUBLISH transitions is ≤ 1.

findings.title: Releasing one guard publishes a hunk that another guard still holds (breaker 'publish', conflict 'keep mine', handoff decline)
findings.scenario: (1) A's human runs a formatter, and the mass-change breaker trips on 180 files. Inside the batch is the stale-buffer revert of B's foo() line. The human answers 'yes, publish the formatting', which releases the breaker, and the whole snapshot goes out. (2) The conflict-policy UI offers 'keep mine' for the x1 conflict. Stage-2 is A's stale buffer, so choosing it also reverts B's fix and C's annotation, and the resolution is treated as human-confirmed, bypassing the revert detector. (3) The holder declines a handoff, the request RETURNS to A, and the push-gate withdrawal is lifted because the claim is gone, but the hunk was also contested.
findings.consequence: A guard-specific 'yes' turns into a blanket publish. Reverts that the other guards were holding go out with a human's apparent consent, although the human was answering a different question.
findings.evidence_detail: Follows from the stores and guards listed in the gap brief, none of which defines composition. x1 (VERIFIED) shows that the stage-2 blob equals the revert hold's H1, so 'keep mine' is exactly the revert.
findings.mitigation: Rule H32: guards compose with AND. Each (hold id, guard) pair is released separately, and a line is published only when every guard on it is released. Rule H33: releasing a SNAPSHOT guard (breaker) re-runs every per-line guard over the batch, and the release prompt shows the residue ('180 files of formatting will publish; 1 hunk in foo() reverts B's fix from 10:01 and stays held'). Rule H34: conflict and quarantine resolutions are candidate outputs. They go through the same revert detector, and the UI states provenance ('keep mine also undoes B's fix (10:01) and C's note (10:05)').
findings.test: Property test: generate hunks with random guard sets, release random subsets, and assert that a published line never carries an unreleased guard. Scenario test: run a formatter over the repo plus one stale revert, choose 'publish formatting', and assert the live ref has the formatting and B's fix.

findings.title: A mass-change breaker that freezes only publishing lets incoming applies write into a stashed or checked-out worktree, so the human's way back (`stash pop`, `checkout`) fails or discards team work
findings.scenario: During a live session A's HEAD and index are still at the base commit, so `git status` lists every live change, including peers'. A's human runs `git stash` to test something. Every live change, including B's work, goes into the stash and the disk returns to base. The breaker trips and publishing stops, but apply continues: B changes bar(), and A's daemon writes it into f.py. The human runs `git stash pop`.
findings.consequence: `git stash pop` exits 1 with "Your local changes to the following files would be overwritten by merge: f.py", and the stash, which holds the team's live state, stays in the stash. Each way out loses something. `checkout -- f.py && stash pop` discards B's newest change from A's disk, and the revert detector then has to catch it. Releasing the breaker publishes the mass revert. Stash-and-forget leaves the team state in a local stash forever.
findings.evidence_detail: sweep/hold/exp_k_stash.py: after stash, 'diff(LA,disk) files: [f.py, g.py]'; A sync applies B2; 'git stash pop exit 1 | error: Your local changes to the following files would be overwritten by merge: f.py'; 'stash list: stash@{0}'. sweep/e17 (sibling) showed stash leaves no marker file.
findings.mitigation: Rule H35: the breaker is a SNAPSHOT hold that freezes both directions. The daemon still fetches but neither applies nor publishes for this worktree, and it posts one board event ('A paused: 2 files reverted to base by git stash'). Rule H36: the breaker clears automatically only when diff(LA, disk) falls back under the threshold, for example after `stash pop`. Otherwise it clears through `/cowork resolve breaker --restore`, which 3-way-restores the team state into the worktree, or `--publish`, which goes through rule H33. It never clears on a timeout. Rule H37: PreToolUse(Bash) denies `git stash`, `checkout --`, `reset --hard` and `restore` from Claude while live, and points to `/cowork pause`. For humans, `/cowork status` explains the pause.
findings.test: Replay exp_k against the daemon. After the stash, assert that no apply and no push happen for N loops. Then run `stash pop` and assert exit 0, then auto-clear, then one catch-up apply that brings in B2, with B2 and A's stash content both present and nothing published in between.

findings.title: Held content stays on disk and the local Claude builds on it, so dependent edits are published while the thing they depend on is held
findings.scenario: Claude on a macOS peer creates `aux.py` (Windows-reserved; sweep/e4 shows `con.py` fails read-tree as 'invalid path' on Windows). The portability gate holds the path after the fact. The same turn edits main.py to `import aux` and calls `aux.parse()`. main.py has no hold, so it is published. A second variant: A's Claude reads f.py, which contains a held revert, assumes `x + 1` is the team's behaviour, and changes callers or tests to match. Those callers publish while the held line does not. A third variant: an Edit adjacent to a held line cannot be separated from it by the merge-mask.
findings.consequence: Every Windows peer receives an import of a module that does not exist, and their tests fail. Their Claudes, following prior-art failure #4 (agents 'repair' unexpected changes), may delete the import or create stubs, which multiplies the damage. In the second variant, tests published by A encode behaviour the team does not have. In the third, Claude's legitimate edit is silently withheld along with the hold.
findings.evidence_detail: The adjacency limitation is VERIFIED: sweep/hold/exp_more.py d2, a Claude edit on the line next to the held line, gives 'merge-mask result: CONFLICT rc=1'. The rest is reasoned from held bytes staying on disk, which the gap brief notes is the norm.
findings.mitigation: Rule H38: any guard whose verdict is computable before the write becomes a PreToolUse denial instead of a hold: portability (reserved names, case or NFC collision, length), scope (generated, LFS, >5 MB) and held-region overlap ±1 (rule H3). The denial text gives Claude a concrete alternative. Rule H39: PostToolUse(Read) and the SessionStart context list ACTIVE holds in the files Claude reads ('f.py line 6 is a LOCAL-ONLY revert held since 10:02; the team has `x + 2  # fix`'). Rule H40: when a hold is created from a Claude-authored change, the same hook tells Claude at once that its change is not shared, so that it neither depends on it nor reports it as done.
findings.test: Hook-harness test: a Write of aux.py is denied with an alternative name; a Read of a file with a hold returns additionalContext naming the hold; an Edit whose old_string touches a held line ±1 is denied. E2E: a scripted Claude turn on peer X that creates aux.py and imports it must leave no `import aux` in the live tree.

findings.title: A hold with no deadline leaves one peer permanently different from the team, and nobody is told until someone else's work depends on that region
findings.scenario: A's human dismisses the first warning ('keep local'). The hold stays ACTIVE on A's disk for days. B keeps editing near it. A's Claude, A's tests and A's builds run against foo() with `x + 1`, while the team runs `x + 2`. A bug report from A ('foo is off by one again') sends B hunting for a regression that exists only on A's PC. The quarantine 'pinned until /cowork resolve' and parked items behave the same way.
findings.consequence: INV-CONVERGE never holds for A, and the difference is invisible to other peers. People and Claudes waste time on phantom bugs and reproduce findings that do not reproduce elsewhere. A hold also never reaches the holder's queue, so decision 7's 'handle it?' flow never fires.
findings.evidence_detail: Follows from 'quarantine pinned until /cowork resolve' and 'each hold has a visible age and escalates' (gap brief) with no escalation endpoint defined.
findings.mitigation: Rule H41 (escalation ladder, values configurable): t0 tells the local Claude and human (statusline + hook context). t+10 min posts one board event to all peers ('A holds a local revert of B's foo() line 6'), and B's Claude is informed when it next touches foo. t+60 min, or at the author's Stop/SessionEnd, turns the hold into a handoff record in the claim holder's or peer author's queue, using decision-7 semantics, with the patch. t+24 h, or at `/cowork stop`, moves it to PARKED: the bytes are removed from disk by a 3-way restore of the team version, and the registry and board copy remain, so the peer converges. Rule H42: `/cowork status` and the board show each peer's 'diverged regions: n (oldest 3 h)'.
findings.test: Simulated clock: create a hold and advance time. Assert the board event happens exactly once at t+10, the queue record at t+60, and PARKED with disk == tip at t+24 h, with the hold still restorable byte-exact from the board.
