findings.title: EOL/BOM/mode normalisation 'holds' modelled as line hunks conflict with every import edit and claim the <imports> pseudo-symbol
findings.scenario: Claude's Write rewrites the 1.3 MB BOM+CRLF Python file without the BOM, or a peer's editor flips EOL. The normaliser keeps the canonical form out of the published blob, which is a hold. If that hold is stored as a PATCH (line 1 changed), the BOM change shares line 1 with the first import. A peer's later edit of line 1 or 2 makes the merge-mask conflict, and the symbol mapper attributes the change to <imports> and claims it.
findings.consequence: A spurious CONFLICTED hold withholds the whole 26k-line file from publishing, so all of A's later edits to it stop propagating. Or A holds a phantom claim on <imports> that blocks every peer's import edits ('deny + note') for something nobody meant to change.
findings.evidence_detail: The BOM is part of line 1's bytes (git does not strip it). Adjacent or same-line changes conflict in xdiff merges (sweep/e5 and hold/d2). The sibling finding eol-renormalization-whole-file-conflict covers the EOL side.
findings.mitigation: Rule H43: hold kinds are distinct. TRANSFORM holds (BOM, EOL, file mode, filter normalisation) are a per-path function applied to every outgoing blob and every disk write. They are never line hunks, never claimed, and never shown as symbol changes. PATH holds (portability, unreadable, scope) replace the outgoing entry with the LA entry. PATCH holds use the 3-way operator. SNAPSHOT holds (breaker) freeze. INCOMING holds (pending) keep a per-path base.
findings.test: Write the big BOM+CRLF file without the BOM and change one function, while a peer changes line 2. Assert the published blob has the BOM, both function edits, and no claim on <imports>, and that no CONFLICTED hold exists.

design_changes: ONE HOLD REGISTRY replaces the seven proposed stores (refs/cowork-held/*, refs/worktree/…/parked*, quarantine .patch files, conflicts/<path>@<peer>, refs/cowork-local/…/conflicts/*, separate board records, and the write ring as a hold store). Location: an append-only commit chain at refs/cowork-local/<b>/holds in the common ref namespace (not refs/worktree), written with update-ref --create-reflog and mirrored into the board ref within one loop, except LOCAL-ONLY kinds. Record fields: id (ULID); kind (PATCH | TRANSFORM | PATH | SNAPSHOT | INCOMING); path(s); H0 and H1 blob oids, plus stage1/2/3 for conflicts; current H0'/H1'; guards {revert, contested, withdrawn, quarantine, conflict, park-join, park-stop, breaker, pending, unreadable, portability, eol-bom, filter-secret}; origin (human, or Claude session id); peer authors affected; created_at; last_rebased_LA; state; escalation level; board_record_oid. Identity is the id. Content hashes are only for dedup and display. Whether a hold is present is answered by computing the rebased 3-way operator, never by matching keys or line ranges.

HOLD STATE MACHINE: DETECTED -> ACTIVE (bytes on disk, masked from S_pub) -> one of: SUBSUMED (rebase gives H1' == LA; auto-close, one event) | CONFLICTED (rebase conflicts; path withheld; conflict stages attached to the same id) | OFFERED (handoff in the holder's or author's queue) -> ACCEPTED (holder published it; requester rebases -> SUBSUMED) or DECLINED -> RETURNED (back to ACTIVE or PARKED at the requester) | PARKED (bytes removed from disk by 3-way restore; registry + board keep them) | RESOLVED_PUBLISH (human command; passes every guard again) | RESOLVED_DISCARD (human command; logged). Transitions happen only on: an apply (rebase every hold), a local write (re-run guards), a human command, the escalation timer, save (rebase onto C), stop (serialize; PARKED or ACTIVE), and start (re-attach from the registry before the first publish). Board transitions are CAS on the board ref, so two stores cannot resolve one id twice.

TWO-TREE LOOP: S_disk (add -A result, stat-valid index) is the only BASE for merge-tree and read-tree -m -u. S_pub = mask(S_disk, holds) is used only for merge-tree(LA, S_pub, TIP) and the push. LA is only ever a fetched remote commit. Per-loop assertion INV-MASK: S_disk == S_pub ⊕ ACTIVE holds (verified by re-applying each hold's (H0', H1') to S_pub), and diff(LA, S_pub) has no line tainted by an ACTIVE hold. On failure, stop publishing and raise doctor; never push S_disk as a fallback.

MASK OPERATORS BY KIND: PATCH -> merge-file -p --object-id <S_disk blob> <H1'> <H0'> after the rebase H0' = LA blob, H1' = merge-file(H0', H0, H1). TRANSFORM -> a deterministic function (BOM, EOL, mode, filter) applied to every outgoing blob and disk write. PATH -> the outgoing entry is the LA entry (or absent). SNAPSHOT -> full freeze of apply and publish. INCOMING -> a per-path base map; release re-merges, never blind-writes. Guards compose with AND; each (id, guard) is released separately; claims never change any operator. Git floor: `merge-file --object-id` needs git >= 2.43 and `merge-tree --write-tree` needs >= 2.38. `/cowork start` refuses on older git and never falls back to file-based merge-file, which gives whole-file conflicts under autocrlf (git-transport report §7).

PER-MECHANISM SPEC (identity | where | on disk | release | (1) peer apply shifts | (2) local Claude claims and edits | (3) incoming touches region | (4) save | (5) re-clone, uninstall, stop | (6) two guards). Revert detector: PATCH/revert | registry + board | yes | human resolve or SUBSUMED | rebase | claim ignored; edits overlapping ±1 denied at PreToolUse; edits ≥1 line away publish | clean -> rebase, same line -> CONFLICTED on the same id | rebase onto C; provenance kept in metadata | survives through the board; stop serializes; uninstall refuses | single id, guard set. Contested set: PATCH/contested | same | yes | the peer's claim released AND not revert-tainted | rebase | local claim never exempts | as revert | as revert | as revert | AND. Push-gate withdrawal (conflict causer): PATCH/withdrawn, OFFERED to the winner's queue | same | yes | winner releases or answers 'go first' | rebase | Claude told its change is unpublished | rebase/CONFLICTED | rebase | board copy | AND. Quarantine pinned: PATCH/quarantine as a blob pair, not a .patch | same | yes until t+24 h, then PARKED | human resolve (3-way) | rebase | deny overlap | rebase/CONFLICTED | rebase | board | AND. Conflict stage-2: PATCH/conflict with stages 1/2/3 | same | no (published version on disk) | 3-way resolve that passes the detectors | rebase stage 1 | n/a | re-merge | rebase | board | attaches to an existing id if H1 matches. Parked at join or stop: PATCH/park | same (never refs/worktree) | no | 3-way restore at start | rebase | n/a | rebase | rebase | board; append-only | AND. Pending locked: INCOMING | registry + board stub | old bytes | lock clears -> 3-way | per-path base | Edit allowed and merged at release | re-merge | the path is excluded from save until released | stub only | AND. Unreadable: PATH/unreadable, LOCAL-ONLY | registry | yes | readable again | n/a | n/a | deferred as INCOMING | excluded from save | stub | AND. Portability: PreToolUse deny; residual (human-made) = PATH/portability | registry + board | yes | rename | n/a | dependents warned | n/a | excluded | board | AND. EOL/BOM: TRANSFORM | registry | yes | disk matches canonical | position-free | never a hunk or claim | n/a | n/a | n/a | AND. Mass-change breaker: SNAPSHOT | registry + board event | yes | auto when the diff drops under threshold, or human --restore/--publish (H33) | frozen | Edits allowed, held | queued | save blocked on this peer | stop -> PARKED snapshot | releasing re-runs all guards.

PROVENANCE ACROSS SAVES: either save writes one commit per contributing author, or the board ref keeps a provenance map (path, line-hash) -> (author, live commit, time) that is not reset at save. The revert detector is per line over that map plus the live chain, with a time window that spans saves. Region-equals-history and reverse-patch-equality detectors are not used.

PRE-WRITE DENIAL OVER POST-WRITE HOLD: any guard computable at PreToolUse (portability, scope or size, held-region overlap ±1, claims) denies with an actionable alternative. Holds are reserved for human edits and for causes that can only be known after the write. PostToolUse(Read) and SessionStart surface ACTIVE holds in files Claude reads.

LIFECYCLE COMMANDS AND REFUSALS: /cowork holds (id, kind, guards, age, state, mirrored?); /cowork hold show <id> (3-way view with provenance); /cowork resolve <id> --publish|--discard|--park|--restore|--handoff. stop, uninstall, --purge and re-clone helpers refuse while unmirrored holds exist, unless --discard-holds=<ids> or --export <dir> (git bundle) is given. `/cowork start` in a fresh clone imports the user's mirrored holds from the board.

INV PROPERTY-TEST EXTENSIONS (seeded generator, 3 peers, file:// remote, real git; ops: Claude Edit with claim, human stale-buffer save, insert or delete 1-40 lines, same-line peer edit, adjacent peer edit, team-revert of a held change, save, daemon kill -9 and restart, stop/start, worktree remove, gc --prune=now, uninstall --purge, re-clone, file lock and unlock, formatter (mass change), git stash/pop, handoff accept/decline, resolve publish/discard/park). Invariants checked after every op. INV-NOLOSS-H: every byte change ever written by a human or Claude is, at all later times, in exactly one of {live tip or saved branch; an ACTIVE or PARKED hold reachable from the REMOTE board within one loop; a RESOLVED_DISCARD event signed by a human command}. INV-NOREVERT-H: no pushed commit deletes or modifies a line whose provenance is another author unless a RESOLVED_PUBLISH event for a hold covering that line exists. INV-MASK: S_disk == S_pub ⊕ ACTIVE holds on every loop, and the published delta == the peer's non-held local edits (independently computed). INV-CONVERGE-H: with no new edits, every peer reaches disk == tip ⊕ its ACTIVE holds within K loops, and disk == tip after T_park. INV-SINGLE: one id per change; ≤1 RESOLVED_PUBLISH per id; every store or view agrees with the board state. INV-AND: no published line carries an unreleased guard. INV-DURABLE: kill -9, worktree remove, gc, purge or re-clone never reduce the set of ACTIVE+PARKED ids visible from the remote board. INV-SECRET: no board or live object contains the content of a LOCAL-ONLY hold. INV-BUDGET: a peer whose only change is an unchanging hold pushes 0 times after the first. INV-RECEIVE: a hold never blocks applying incoming changes to other paths or to other regions of the same path.
open_questions: The gap brief quotes the contested-set rule ('exempt if a local session holds a claim on that symbol'), the stores and the revert detector only in summary. My models reconstruct them (incremental detection, pinned holds, blame-based provenance). The orchestrator should confirm each reconstruction against the owning lens (human-git-lifecycle, negotiation, editor-fs, git-integrity, product-ux-ops).

Should a stale-buffer revert hold ever be PARKED automatically (bytes removed from the human's open file), given that editors then show 'file changed on disk' prompts and a careless 'keep mine' rewrites the hold? The alternative is to stay ACTIVE indefinitely, which violates INV-CONVERGE.

How does save attribute per symbol: per-author commits (blame keeps provenance) or trailers in one commit (blame loses it)? This decides whether rule H13 needs a separate provenance map in the board ref.
Is the 'conflict causer' push-gate withdrawal meant to leave the causer's edit on disk (ACTIVE hold) or remove it (PARKED)? This changes what the causer's Claude sees when it re-reads the file.

Board mirroring publishes teammates' unpublished, possibly half-finished work to all collaborators of the private repo. Do users accept that every held change is visible to the team, with LOCAL-ONLY kinds as the exception?

Can a marker under .claude/ reliably make Claude Code's worktree auto-cleanup treat a worktree with PARKED items as 'has work'? Docs say it checks changed or untracked files, so the marker must be untracked and not ignored. Needs a spike against v2.1.2xx.
Escalation timer defaults (10 min board event, 60 min handoff, 24 h park) and whether an ACTIVE hold should block `save` on the holder's PC or only be listed in the save report.

gapResults.lens: gap:Publication units versus logical change units (cross-file and cross-symbol atomicity)

findings.title: Debounce and the governor publish one Claude turn in pieces: peers run code that is half of a signature change
findings.scenario: Alice's Claude makes one logical change in one turn. E1 edits pricing.py: compute_price gains a required 'currency' and a new constant CURRENCY_DEFAULT is added. About 40 s later E2 edits orders.py and E3 edits reports.py to update the callers. The daemon's quiet period ends while Claude is generating the next tool call, so push #1 carries E1 only. E2 and E3 ride push #2, one or more governor slots later. Bob and Carol fetch push #1. merge-tree exits 0 and read-tree -m -u exits 0 on both PCs. If Claude happened to edit the caller first, push #1 carries E2 only.
findings.consequence: Between push #1 and push #2, every peer's tree is broken, although no hunk conflicted. With E1 first, unittest fails with TypeError: compute_price() missing 'currency'. With E2 first, an ImportError kills the whole test module and any app that imports orders. py_compile passes in both cases. In C#, the caller-first split fails dotnet build with CS1501. Real turn timings make this the normal case: the gap between consecutive cross-file edits has a median of 41 s, and 89% of gaps exceed 10 s, so no debounce setting avoids it. In the simulation of the approved policy, peers saw 100% of multi-file turns half-done, for a median of 145 s and a p90 of 627 s.
findings.evidence_detail: sweep/atom/x1_debounce_split.py, x1.log: Bob's merge-tree 0, read-tree 0, py_compile 0. unittest gives 'FAILED (errors=2) TypeError' with E1 first and 'ImportError cannot import name CURRENCY_DEFAULT' with E2 first, and passes after push #2. x4c (C#): CS1501, then build 0 after push #2. x11_gaps.py over this PC's own transcripts (1,901 editing turns, aggregates only): 65% of editing turns touch 2 or more files; cross-file edit gap p50 41 s, p90 148 s; 57% of gaps contain a Bash/PowerShell call. x12_sim.py: policy P0 gives 100% half-done, exposure p50 145 s / p90 627 s.
findings.mitigation: Rule PUB-1: the unit of publication is the change-set (CS): every file effect of one turn of one session. Its id is session_id plus a turn epoch that advances at Stop/StopFailure; prompt_id is recorded alongside when present. The daemon publishes a CS's code only when the CS is CLOSED (Stop) or at a GREEN CHECKPOINT. A green checkpoint is a PostToolUse (not PostToolUseFailure) of a Bash/PowerShell command that matches the repo's configured `checks` patterns, such as pytest, dotnet build or npm test. Once 300 s (the default cap) have passed since the oldest unpublished hunk, the CS-so-far is published with trailer state=wip, but only if T0 checks pass, and a board 'incomplete' record is posted (see provenance-rule-blind-to-withdrawal-deferral-save). Claims are not held: board-only pushes carry them in seconds. Human edits form a CS closed by a 20 s quiet period or `/cowork done`, and are flagged as human WIP. Measured cost (x12, pool budget): edit-to-publish latency rises from p50 3 s / p90 12 s to p50 96 s / p90 266 s. Half-done exposure falls from 100% to 3%. Claim-to-board stays at p50 8 s. Pushes rise from 2.0 to 2.4 per minute against the 6/min budget. The cost is visibility latency, not push budget. Checkpoint publishes carry trailer state=checkpoint seq=N, which declares a prefix of the CS; receivers materialize them by default. state=wip publishes are materialized only on opt-in. Whether `publish: checkpoint` or `publish: live` is the team default is the user's call, because it departs from decision 3's 'tens of seconds when busy' (see open_questions).
findings.test: Harness (lib.py) replays a 3-edit turn with 40 s gaps through simulated PreToolUse/PostToolUse/Stop events, and a receiver runs unittest after every apply. Assert that no live commit whose trailer lacks `wip` contains a strict non-empty subset of the CS's hunks. Assert that the receiver's tests never fail between the first and last apply. Repeat with the edit order reversed and with the C# fixture (dotnet build).

findings.title: Per-hunk push-gate withdrawal publishes a tree that never existed (new signature, old call site); the sender stays green while everyone else is red
findings.scenario: Alice has finished CS-A on disk: the pricing signature, the checkout call and the summarize call. Bob's claim on orders.py:checkout reached the board first, inside the propagation window, so Alice is the 'conflict causer'. Her push gate withdraws only the hunk inside checkout and publishes the rest. The withdrawn hunk becomes a handoff to Bob, delivered at his Stop and applied only when he accepts it.
findings.consequence: Carol and Bob receive pricing.py with the 3-argument signature and checkout with the 2-argument call. merge exits 0, apply exits 0, py_compile exits 0 and import works, but unittest fails with TypeError. In C#, dotnet build fails with CS7036. Alice's own disk still holds the whole CS, so her tests and build pass and her Claude believes all is well. Unlike a debounce split, this breakage lasts until the holder finishes his turn and accepts the patch, which can be minutes to hours. Every peer's tests, build and dev server stay broken for that time, and a save taken meanwhile is broken too.
findings.evidence_detail: sweep/atom/x2_x3_withdraw.py, x2x3.log: 'push-gate orders.py: withdrew 1 hunk(s) [(5, checkout)]'. Carol: merge-tree 0, read-tree 0, py_compile ok, import ok, then 'TypeError compute_price() missing 1 required positional argument: currency'. Alice's unittest passes. x4_csharp.py X4a: Carol's build exits 1 with CS7036; Alice's build exits 0.
findings.mitigation: Rule GATE-1: withdrawal is all-or-nothing per CS. If any hunk of a CS falls in a foreign published claim, the whole CS is HELD: none of its hunks is published, and Alice's disk keeps all of them. On the sender the granularity is whole FILES. Every path touched by a held CS is pinned at its last-published blob in the outgoing tree. Any other work on this PC that lands in a pinned file (a later CS, a human save, a second session) is held with it. The daemon never subtracts a held CS's hunks out of a file, because that is the -U0 surgery shown to delete and duplicate functions (intra-file-withdrawal-mangles-file). GATE-2 (dependents): a later CS of the same session is held too if it touches a path of a held CS or references a symbol whose signature the held CS changed. A board record `held{cs, paths, blocking_claim, since}` turns this into the requirement-4 conversation. 'May I go first?' becomes a concrete request: let held CS-A land, including its one hunk in your symbol. If the holder agrees, his daemon 3-way merges that hunk into his working copy. GATE-3: a hold older than 10 min re-prompts the causer's Claude to wait or hand off. Push cost: zero. Latency cost: the CS's non-conflicting parts are delayed until the hold resolves. That is deliberate: nothing broken is published.
findings.test: X2 fixture with Bob's claim on checkout published before Alice's push. Assert the live ref tree shows no change to pricing.py, orders.py or reports.py while CS-A is held, and that Carol's unittest stays green throughout. After Bob releases the claim, assert that one live commit contains all three files and the tests pass. Variant: Alice's next turn edits orders.py:refund and imports CURRENCY_DEFAULT; assert that this CS is held too (GATE-2).

findings.title: Save that splices ACTIVE symbols out writes a branch commit that no PC ever ran, and it fails
findings.scenario: (a) Alice's CS-A (closed) changed compute_price and checkout. summarize was handed to Bob, who is still ACTIVE in it; it holds the call-site update plus his own WIP. Someone runs /cowork save, which keeps the base text for ACTIVE symbols. (b) Alice is ACTIVE on a new pricing.tax(), and Carol's closed change in checkout imports and calls tax(). Save excludes tax.
findings.consequence: On every PC the live tree passes its tests, but the saved commit fails. (a) gives a TypeError in summarize. (b) gives ImportError 'cannot import name tax', which kills the whole test module. The broken commit lands on the real branch, so CI, PR builds and anyone who pulls see a red main. The per-symbol attribution in the commit points at the saver. Excluding whole change-sets instead of symbols fixes (a) but not (b), because (b) is a semantic dependency between two CSs.
findings.evidence_detail: sweep/atom/x5_deferral_save_cas.py, x5x6x7.log. X6a: 'live tree on every PC: unittest OK'; the saved commit, tested in a temp worktree, gives 'TypeError compute_price() missing currency'. X6b: live tree OK; the saved commit gives 'ImportError: cannot import name tax from pricing'.
findings.mitigation: Rule SAVE-1: never synthesize a tree at save; only existing live commits are candidates. SAVE-2: walk back from the live tip, up to N=20 commits. For each candidate, run a configurable smoke check in a throwaway `git worktree add --detach <candidate>`, using the import/compile/build/test commands from .cowork/config plus T0 checks. Prefer the newest passing candidate whose trailers show no open or wip CS. Otherwise take the newest passing candidate, including checkpoint or wip states. If none passes, refuse and show the failing output. A whole-team 'nobody mid-turn' commit is rare with 4 busy PCs (turn p50 341 s vs 20-120 s idle), so it cannot be the only acceptable candidate. SAVE-3: the attribution trailer lists the CS ids included and their states. Measured cost per candidate tried: worktree add 0.49-0.51 s for 3,001 files plus the 1.34 MB file, worktree remove about 0.16 s, plus the check command. No pushes beyond the branch push.
findings.test: X6a/X6b fixtures. Run save. Assert that the branch is either unchanged (refusal) or points at a commit whose tree equals some live commit's tree and whose smoke check passes in a fresh worktree. Assert that no saved tree differs from every live tree.

findings.title: Withdrawing -U0 hunks inside one file during re-indent refactors duplicates or deletes functions, causes C# syntax errors, and touches non-foreign symbols
findings.scenario: Alice's single Edit (or Write) does one of these refactors: wraps f, g and h into class Ops; unwraps a class into functions; puts two functions under an `if` guard; or converts a C# file from a block-scoped to a file-scoped namespace. A foreign claim on one symbol arrived in the window, so the gate reverts the -U0 hunks that overlap that symbol's base line range.
findings.consequence: git's line-matching hunks do not line up with symbol boundaries when indentation changes. Python results: `def g` is duplicated and Ops.h is gone (AttributeError); or g is lost entirely, with neither the old nor the new version in the file; or f is duplicated when the foreign claim was on g, so a symbol nobody claimed was altered. All of these compile, so a syntax gate passes them. C# results: CS1513 '} expected' with the Compute header line duplicated, and CS1022. Each Python file merged and applied cleanly on peers. A lost function is published to everyone and is one save away from the branch.
findings.evidence_detail: sweep/atom/x3b_explore.py, x3b.log: across 5 refactors and every choice of foreign symbol, 0 py_compile failures, but 'unwrap_class_to_functions foreign=Ops.h defs=[f,h] MISSING=[g]', 'guard_block foreign=g DUPLICATED=[f]' and 'wrap_into_class foreign=g DUPLICATED=[g]'. x2x3.log (published via the daemon, applied with merge-tree/read-tree 0): 'cannot import name Ops' and 'Ops object has no attribute h'. x4.log X4b: build fails with CS1513 and CS1022, and the Compute header appears twice in the published Pricing.cs.
findings.mitigation: Rule GATE-4: never withdraw below a tool_use. If any hunk of a tool_use touches a foreign claim, the whole CS is held (GATE-1). If a partial file must ever be produced, for example by saving a WIP CS, run T0 checks on it before it leaves the PC. T0 here means a tree-sitter parse with no ERROR/MISSING nodes, plus symbol accounting. Symbol accounting: the published file's definitions must equal the base definitions, plus those added by kept hunks, minus those deleted by kept hunks, with no duplicate qualnames. Any mismatch keeps the CS held. Cost: ast and symbol table take 397 ms for a 1.34 MB file and milliseconds for small files.
findings.test: Table-driven test over x3b's 5 refactors plus the C# namespace conversion, once for each choice of foreign symbol. Run the gate and assert the published file is either its base version or Alice's full version, never a third text. Assert that symbol accounting rejects every case listed in x3b.log.

findings.title: Per-path deferred apply (tree surgery) leaves the receiver's disk with half a change-set, exactly while its own Claude is about to run tests
findings.scenario: Alice publishes CS-A whole, in one push. On Bob's PC, orders.py is pending because Bob's Claude holds a PreToolUse fence on it, either mid-Edit in refund or waiting at a permission prompt. An IDE or Excel lock, or a 'hot' path, has the same effect. The git-integrity proposal applies M' = M with the pending path taken from S, so pricing.py and reports.py land and orders.py does not. In a variant, pricing.py is the fenced path.
findings.consequence: Bob's disk ends up with either the new signature and the old checkout (TypeError) or the new orders.py and the old pricing.py (ImportError, which kills the test module and any app import). The live ref is consistent, so the breakage exists only on Bob's PC, and no board record or blame explains it. The fenced file is the one Bob's Claude is editing, and its next step is usually running tests: 57% of cross-file edit gaps contain a Bash call. It sees a failure in its own file and tries to fix Alice's call site, which is claimed, so the edit is denied. It may then open a needless 'conflict' negotiation. A fence held by a pending permission prompt, or a lock held by Excel, stretches this from milliseconds to minutes or hours.
findings.evidence_detail: sweep/atom/x5_deferral_save_cas.py, x5x6x7.log. X5a: 'deferred [orders.py] via tree surgery', read-tree 0, unittest 'TypeError ... currency'. X5b: 'deferred [pricing.py]', 'ImportError: cannot import name CURRENCY_DEFAULT', test module failed to import. A permission denial fires PreToolUse but neither PostToolUse nor PostToolUseFailure (DOCUMENTED, https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#posttoolusefailure), so a fence can stay open.
findings.mitigation: Rule APPLY-1 (reconciles with git-integrity's per-path tolerance): keep the tree surgery, but compute the pending set as a closure. Pending = every path of every incoming CS that touches any locked, fenced, unmaterializable or colliding path, repeated until nothing changes. Apply M' = M with the whole closure taken from S. CS membership comes from commit trailers (see cs-manifest-must-ride-code-commit). APPLY-2: while a closure is pending, the status line shows 'behind on CS-A (waiting for orders.py)'. When a Bash/PowerShell tool call starts on this PC, PreToolUse additionalContext says 'tests run against a tree without CS-A'. APPLY-3: a fence closes on PostToolUse, PostToolUseFailure, PermissionDenied or the session's next PreToolUse, with a 120 s cap. Cost: zero pushes. The other files of a deferred CS wait as long as the deferral, typically one Edit (under 1 s).
findings.test: X5a/X5b fixtures. Hold a fence on one path and run the apply. Assert that either none or all of CS-A's three paths changed on Bob's disk, and that Bob's unittest result equals its pre-apply result. Release the fence and assert all three land in one apply. Repeat with a FileShare.Read lock instead of a fence.

findings.title: After a lease reject, the clean re-merge publishes a tree where CS-A's own promise ('all callers updated') is false, and nobody is told
findings.scenario: Alice's CS-A updates every caller of compute_price that exists when she writes it. Meanwhile Bob adds a new reorder() that calls compute_price(qty, unit); it is a free symbol, so there is no claim conflict, and he pushes first. Alice's lease push is rejected. She refetches, merge-tree exits 0, read-tree exits 0, and she pushes.
findings.consequence: The live tree now has a new caller with the old arity, and Carol's reorder() raises TypeError. Region-detect's soft warning ('callers of S with a pending breaking change') cannot fire. When Bob wrote reorder, Alice's change was unpublished, and when Alice re-merged, the merge was textually clean. Both Claudes believe their work is correct, and the break surfaces later on a third PC.
findings.evidence_detail: sweep/atom/x5_deferral_save_cas.py, x5x6x7.log X7: 'alice: push REJECTED', 'merge-tree exit=0', 'read-tree -m -u exit=0', 'push OK', 'CAROL reorder() -> TypeError'. An ast caller-arity scan of the merged tree reports ['orders.py:14'].
findings.mitigation: Rule GATE-5: for every symbol whose signature the outgoing CS changes in a breaking way (per the region-detect classifier), re-run the caller scan on the MERGED tree after every merge, including re-merges after a CAS reject. The scan is `git grep -w -F name`, filtered by tree-sitter/ast, then an arity and keyword compatibility check. If new incompatible callers appear, the CS stays held. The author's Claude is told through PostToolUse, or through an inbox message when idle: 'reorder() in orders.py (by Bob) calls compute_price with the old signature: update it (unclaimed) or hand off (claimed)'. Fixing it extends the same CS. Cost: zero pushes. Each publish that carries a breaking change costs about 80 ms of grep (region-detect report) plus parsing the hit files (397 ms for a 1.34 MB file).
findings.test: X7 fixture. Assert that Alice's daemon does not push the re-merged tree while the scan reports orders.py:14, and that the push happens, with Carol green, once the hit is fixed. Negative control: if Bob's new caller already uses 3 arguments, the push happens immediately.

findings.title: Every apply restarts peers' dev servers, a split CS keeps them down for the split's duration, and dotnet watch hot reload crashes the app
findings.scenario: Bob runs `dotnet watch` (default hot reload) or `flask run --debug` while his daemon applies the team's pushes. Push #1 changes only the caller, and push #2 changes the provider. Later a provider-only change arrives: Pricing.Compute gains 'region' before Orders.cs catches up.
findings.consequence: Under dotnet watch hot reload, the caller-only apply gives 'Unable to apply changes' (CS1501) and the app keeps running old code. The provider-only apply leaves a tree that does not build, yet dotnet watch reported 'C# and Razor changes applied in 17ms'. The app then died with System.TypeLoadException 'Invalid_Token.0x02000040' at Pricing.Compute and stayed down until the next file change; this reproduced twice. With --no-hot-reload, every apply kills, rebuilds and restarts the app with a new PID, and on a split the app stays down until the other half arrives. Under withdrawal, that wait is the whole hold. Under Flask, every apply is a restart (6 restarts for 6 applies in 23 s, with visible DOWN gaps). Half a CS gives HTTP 500 on every request until the CS completes. There was no crash loop, because Flask loads lazily under the reloader. Peers lose in-memory state at the team's apply rate.
findings.evidence_detail: sweep/atom/x9_dotnet_watch.py, x9_hot.log lines 29-68, and x9_nohot.out (PIDs 26980->9784->9304; 'The build failed' with CS1501 and CS7036). x8b_flask.py, x8b.log ('after push#1 ... 500', 'burst: 6 reloader restarts for 6 applies in 23s'). uvicorn --reload stalled in the headless harness because it needs a real console, so it is not used as evidence. The explanation that hot reload checks diagnostics only for changed documents is REASONED.
findings.mitigation: Rule APPLY-4: receivers materialize only whole CSs (PUB-1, APPLY-1), so a dev server never sees a provider-only or caller-only state. APPLY-5: coalesce applies. Apply at most once per `apply_min_interval` (default 10 s), batching every closed CS that arrived in between. Users can set `apply: on-idle`, which applies only when no Bash/PowerShell tool call is running and no file was saved in the last 5 s. APPLY-6: materialize state=closed and state=checkpoint CSs by default; materialize state=wip or checks=fail only if the user opted in. Cost: at most 10 s of extra visibility latency and no pushes. Restarts drop from one per push to one per batch.
findings.test: Run harnesses x9 and x8b with the daemon in checkpoint mode. Replay the 4-push C# sequence and assert zero TypeLoadException, zero 'build failed' lines, and fewer restarts than CSs. For Flask, assert no HTTP 500 during the run. Count restarts per hour under the x12 replay timings.

findings.title: A snapshot taken between truncate and write captures a 0-byte version of a file and would publish it to everyone
findings.scenario: A tool writes a file in place, for example with Node fs.writeFileSync, as many editors and Node tools do. Whether Claude Code's Edit/Write writes this way is UNKNOWN. The daemon's `git add -A` runs every 2-3 s and happens to read big.py after the truncate but before the data is written.
findings.consequence: The snapshot blob is empty. Once published, the team's 1.3 MB file is empty on every peer for at least one governor slot. It still passes py_compile, but every `from big import ...` fails. A peer with local edits in that file gets a whole-file conflict. A peer's Claude that reads the file in that window sees an empty file and may recreate or 'restore' it, colliding with the real content arriving next. Side effect: on Windows, 511 of 824 in-place writes failed with UNKNOWN (-4094) while git had the file open. That was a tight loop, so real-rate exposure is lower, but an Edit failing because the daemon is reading the file is plausible.
findings.evidence_detail: sweep/atom/x13_torn.py, x13.log: 'snapshots=416 torn_blobs=5' (blobs equal to neither version, size 0); 'torn blob size=0 (full=1340803) py_compile exit=0'; 'writes 824 failed 511 {UNKNOWN:511}'.
findings.mitigation: Rule SNAP-1: the daemon does not re-read a path under a write fence and keeps its previous blob. A write fence runs from PreToolUse to PostToolUse of Edit/Write/MultiEdit/NotebookEdit/Bash/PowerShell in any live session on this PC. SNAP-2 (stability, for writes without hooks): a changed path is publishable only if (size, mtime_ns, blob oid) are identical across two reads at least 1 s apart. SNAP-3: a change from non-empty to empty, or a shrink of more than 50%, is publishable only if it is stable across two snapshot cycles AND attributable. Attributable means a Write tool_use with empty or short content, a deletion, or a human save seen twice. Cost: about one extra snapshot interval (2-3 s) of latency for writes without hooks. No pushes.
findings.test: x13 harness: an in-place writer alternates two versions while the snapshot loop runs. Assert that every blob that would be published is one of the two versions. Then inject a writer that truncates, sleeps, then writes, and assert the empty blob is never published.

findings.title: The recent-provenance 'don't fix' rule cannot fire for breaks created by withdrawal, deferral or save, and its time window expires while the break persists
findings.scenario: After a withdrawal (the X2 state), Carol's Claude runs the tests and gets a TypeError at orders.py:5. Its hook looks up provenance for the failing line. The same happens with a deferral on Bob's PC (X5) and after pulling a spliced save (X6).
findings.consequence: Blame on the live ref attributes the failing line to the BASE commit. Only the import line belongs to Alice's publish, and the breaking change sits in pricing.py, which the traceback mentions only as the callee. A line-keyed 'recently synced from a teammate' rule stays silent. A deferral break exists only on Bob's disk, so the ref holds nothing to attribute. A save break is attributed to the saver. A withdrawal break lasts until the holder's Stop and acceptance, longer than any 'recent' window. Expected behaviour (REASONED): peers' Claudes 'fix' code that is not broken in anyone's intent. They edit test expectations, or add a default `currency=None` or a shim in unclaimed code. When Bob later applies Alice's handoff patch, the fix is doubled and the API semantics drift. Or they open conflict negotiations about phantom conflicts, which turns requirement 4 into noise.
findings.evidence_detail: The mechanism is VERIFIED: in x2x3.log, `git blame -s refs/cowork-remote/code -- orders.py` attributes line 5 ('total = compute_price(qty, unit)') to ^e8cc9b4 (base) and line 1 to da597484 (Alice). The rule's exact definition comes from round 1, which this lens did not have. Agent reaction: prior-art Top-15 #4 ('agents repair unexpected changes', mcp_agent_mail #272).
findings.mitigation: Rule NOTE-1: the system writes a board record for every split it knowingly creates: a capped WIP publish, a hold whose parts are visible elsewhere, a receiver closure deferral, or a save that includes WIP. The record is `incomplete{cs, owner, affected_paths, affected_symbols (callee + known callers), expected_errors (e.g. 'missing 1 required positional argument: currency', CS7036), resolves_when}`. It lives as long as the CS's state, not by a clock. NOTE-2: a PostToolUseFailure hook on Bash/PowerShell matches the error text against active records by path, symbol and error signature. (PostToolUseFailure is documented to start with 'Exit code N' and to support additionalContext.) On a match it injects: 'Expected failure: Alice's CS-A is incomplete here (waiting for Bob on orders.py:checkout). Do not edit tests or add shims. It resolves when <resolves_when>.' NOTE-3: a PreToolUse on Edit/Write of an affected symbol by a third party adds the same context. Cost: no pushes beyond the board record, which rides the next board push.
findings.test: Hook unit test. Feed the X2 PostToolUseFailure payload (Bash 'python -m unittest', error containing the TypeError) together with the board record, and assert additionalContext names CS-A and its owner. Feed the same error with the record resolved and assert nothing is injected. Feed an unrelated TypeError and assert nothing is injected.

findings.title: Restoring the author's foreign-symbol hunks at PostToolUse leaves the author's own disk with half a CS and steers its Claude into API-bending workarounds
findings.scenario: Alice's Claude edits the checkout call site. Bob's claim on checkout arrived between Alice's PreToolUse and PostToolUse, so her PostToolUse restores the hunk on her disk. Her earlier Edit already changed the pricing signature. Her Claude then runs the tests.
findings.consequence: Alice's disk now holds the same tree that X2 published, so the tests fail with TypeError. Her Claude cannot edit checkout (denied), so the cheapest path to green lies inside its own claim: make `currency` optional or add `compute_price_legacy`. That publishes a weaker API to everyone. Later Bob applies the handoff patch, and both the default and the explicit argument exist. If the restore is silent, Claude's model of the file is also wrong, so its next Edit's old_string misses or matches somewhere unexpected.
findings.evidence_detail: The resulting tree is the one VERIFIED in x2x3.log (TypeError). The agent behaviour is inferred.
findings.mitigation: Rule POST-1: PostToolUse never rewrites the author's disk. The hunk stays local, the CS becomes HELD (GATE-1), and the hook returns `decision: block` with the reason: 'your edit to orders.py:checkout overlaps Bob's claim (published at T). It is kept on your disk but not published. CS-A is held until Bob answers. Do not work around it by changing compute_price's signature.' If Bob accepts, the hunk is merged into his copy; if he releases the claim, CS-A lands unchanged.
findings.test: Hook-level test: simulate the claim arriving between Pre and Post. Assert that the file bytes after PostToolUse equal the bytes Claude wrote, that the board shows held{CS-A}, and that the hook output contains decision:block and the claim holder's name.

findings.title: A Bash/PowerShell command is a multi-file transaction: snapshots split codemods mid-run, and applies landing mid-test cause spurious failures
findings.scenario: (a) Claude runs a codemod, a formatter (`dotnet format`, `ruff --fix`), a generator or `npm install` that rewrites dozens of files over several seconds, and the 2-3 s snapshot fires in the middle. (b) On a receiver, Claude's `pytest` has already imported pricing.py when the daemon applies a CS. The test process then imports the new orders.py, which needs the new pricing.
findings.consequence: In (a), a partial codemod is published. Peers see half of a rename, which gives the same ImportError and TypeError class as debounce-splits-every-multifile-turn. In (b), a test run that mixes versions fails even though the apply itself was atomic, and the receiving Claude debugs a failure that never existed. A permission denial fires PreToolUse but no Post hook (DOCUMENTED), so a fence opened at PreToolUse can stay open forever.
findings.evidence_detail: The split mechanism is the same as in x1, which is VERIFIED: add -A captures whatever is on disk. Hook facts: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#posttoolusefailure ('Permission denials fire PreToolUse but not this event').
findings.mitigation: Rule TXN-1: each Bash/PowerShell tool call of a live session is a transaction on its own PC. From PreToolUse until PostToolUse, PostToolUseFailure or PermissionDenied, the daemon neither snapshots the worktree nor applies to it. The cap is 120 s, and a run_in_background call closes when the tool returns. Fetch and merge continue in memory. Writes after the cap, or from background processes, form a 'background' CS flagged WIP. TXN-2: an apply waits for the transaction to end, so a test run sees one tree. Cost: publication and apply are delayed by the command's duration, up to the cap. No pushes.
findings.test: Codemod fixture: write 30 files with 100 ms spacing between a simulated PreToolUse and PostToolUse while the snapshot loop runs. Assert that no live commit has 0 < k < 30 of the files changed. Receiver: inside a Bash transaction, a script imports pricing, sleeps 2 s, then imports orders. An apply arriving during the sleep must wait. Assert no ImportError.

findings.title: Holding only the conflicted CS while publishing the author's next CS publishes code that depends on unpublished code
findings.scenario: CS-A (the pricing signature plus CURRENCY_DEFAULT) is held because of Bob's claim. In her next turn, Alice's Claude adds a new function in orders.py, an unclaimed symbol, that imports CURRENCY_DEFAULT and calls the 3-argument compute_price. Nothing blocks CS-B, so the gate publishes it.
findings.consequence: Peers get an orders.py that imports a name not present on the live ref. The ImportError kills the whole module and the test module. This is the X1b state, here created by the fix for withdrawal rather than by debounce, and it lasts for the whole hold.
findings.evidence_detail: The resulting kind of tree is VERIFIED in x1.log X1b ('ImportError: cannot import name CURRENCY_DEFAULT from pricing', merge 0 / apply 0). The hold policy itself was not run, so this is REASONED.
findings.mitigation: GATE-2, as stated in hunk-withdrawal-publishes-signature-without-callers. A later CS of the same session is held if it touches any path of a held CS, or if its hunks reference a name whose definition or signature exists only in a held CS. The check intersects the names added or changed by held CSs (a symbol table diff) with the identifiers the new CS's hunks reference (tree-sitter identifiers, plus imports). GATE-6: after 3 dependent holds or 10 min, the causer's Claude is prompted (requirement 4) to ask the holder or restructure its work. Cost: zero pushes. A dependent CS stays invisible until the hold resolves.
findings.test: Hold CS-A as in the X2 setup, then make CS-B use CURRENCY_DEFAULT. Assert that CS-B is not on the live ref until CS-A lands, and that Carol's import of orders never fails during the hold. Control: a CS-B that touches only an unrelated file publishes normally.

findings.title: Change-set membership kept only on the board ref cannot drive atomic applies, because code and board are not always pushed or fetched together
findings.scenario: The daemon records on the board ref which hunks and paths belong to which CS. On Azure DevOps (no --atomic), the code push succeeds while the board push fails or arrives later. Alternatively, a receiver's fetch sees the new code tip before the board tip, since they are two refs. The receiver must decide what to defer (APPLY-1) and what is WIP (APPLY-6).
findings.consequence: Without membership, the receiver falls back to per-path behaviour and materializes half a CS (receiver-path-deferral-materializes-half-cs), or it treats WIP as closed and crashes dev servers (dev-servers-restart-and-crash-on-split-apply). Save cannot tell which live commits are closed states.
findings.evidence_detail: Azure DevOps does not support --atomic (git-transport report §2, Microsoft Q&A link). Code and board are two refs fetched together, but the board can lag when they are pushed one after the other.
findings.mitigation: Rule MAN-1: every code-ref commit carries one trailer per CS it includes: `Cowork-CS: <cs-id> state=closed|checkpoint|wip seq=<n> author=<peer> paths=<count> hunks=<sha1 of sorted path:blob pairs> checks=pass|fail|skipped`. Being part of the commit makes the trailer atomic with the content. The board keeps only claims, holds and negotiation. MAN-2: a receiver that finds a code commit without trailers (an old peer version) treats it as one CS covering all its paths, with state=wip.
findings.test: Push only the code ref (board push disabled) from Alice with a 2-path CS while Bob has one of the paths fenced. Assert that Bob defers both paths using the trailer alone. Strip the trailers and assert the whole commit is deferred as one unit.

findings.title: A py_compile or syntax-only smoke gate catches none of the Python breaks; only import, arity and symbol checks do
findings.scenario: A team adopts 'run py_compile on changed files before publishing or saving' as its safety net against split change-sets.
findings.consequence: Every Python failure in this sweep passed py_compile: the TypeError splits (x1a, x2, x5a, x6a, x7), the ImportError splits (x1b, x5b, x6b), the duplicated or lost functions (x3b), and even the torn 0-byte file (x13). The gate gives false assurance. C# breaks are caught by `dotnet build`, which takes about 1 s incrementally on the fixture (REASONED: much longer on the real solution).
findings.evidence_detail: x1.log, x2x3.log, x3b.log and x5x6x7.log show 'py_compile -> exit=0' alongside each failure; x13.log shows 'torn blob ... py_compile exit=0'. x10.log costs: compile() 280 ms, ast plus symbol table 397 ms for 1.34 MB, py_compile subprocess 402 ms. x4.log: dotnet build 0.8-1.0 s.
findings.mitigation: Rule CHK-1 defines two tiers. T0 runs in-daemon on every publish and is cheap. It covers: a tree-sitter parse with no ERROR nodes on changed files; symbol accounting (intra-file-withdrawal-mangles-file); caller-arity for breaking signature changes (cas-remerge-breaks-cs-invariant); and a guard against non-empty to empty changes (torn-snapshot-publishes-empty-file). T1 runs at green checkpoints and at save: the repo's configured import/build/test command, in a temp worktree for save. T0's measured cost stays under 0.5 s even for the 1.3 MB file, and T1 adds no pushes.
findings.test: Run T0 over the published trees of x1, x2, x3b, x5, x6, x7 and x13. Assert that each tree is flagged (by symbol accounting, caller-arity or the import check) or held, and that py_compile alone flags none of them.

findings.title: When read-tree -m -u fails mid-write because a file is locked, the other files of the same CS are already on disk
findings.scenario: Bob's daemon applies CS-A (pricing.py, orders.py, reports.py), which arrived in ONE atomic push. Another process holds orders.py open with FileShare.Read: an IDE, a test runner or antivirus, or Excel for an xlsx in the same CS. read-tree -m -u passes its up-to-date check, writes the other files, then fails to replace orders.py.
findings.consequence: Bob's disk holds half the CS, so his dev server, tests and Claude see the same TypeError and ImportError states as above. The private index is not updated, so the next snapshot may also mistake the written files for Bob's own edits (git-integrity lens).
findings.evidence_detail: sweep/atom/x14_lock.py, x14.log: orders.py held via PowerShell [IO.File]::Open(path,'Open','Read','Read'). merge-tree 0; read-tree -m -u exit 128 "unable to unlink old 'orders.py': Invalid argument". Bob's disk: pricing.py NEW, reports.py NEW, orders.py old. LAST was not advanced, and unittest fails with TypeError. Same mechanism as the git-integrity sweep's e2.
findings.mitigation: Rule APPLY-7: before read-tree, preflight every path in the CS closure by opening it for write with exclusive sharing (Windows) and closing it again. A path that fails is treated as pending, and APPLY-1's closure is recomputed. If read-tree still fails partway, roll back: rewrite every path of the affected CSs from S (the pre-apply snapshot blobs, via checkout-index from the S index), then mark the closure pending. Cost: one open/close per path, a few ms. No pushes.
findings.test: 2-file CS with one file held by a helper process via FileShare.Read. Assert that after the apply attempt both files are either at the new version or at the old one, that the status shows the CS pending, and that it lands in one step once the lock is released.

design_changes: Make the CHANGE-SET (CS) the unit of publication, apply, withdrawal and save, instead of the hunk, path or symbol. A CS is every file effect of one turn of one session, from UserPromptSubmit or an inbox-started turn to Stop/StopFailure. Its id is session_id plus a turn epoch; prompt_id (documented, v2.1.196+, absent before the first input) is recorded when present. Subagent tool calls belong to the parent's CS. Nothing is ever split below one tool_use or one Bash/PowerShell call. Human edits form a CS closed by a 20 s quiet period or `/cowork done`. Reason: 65% of real editing turns touch 2 or more files, with a median of 41 s between cross-file edits (x11), so every finer unit publishes half-changes (x1, x2, x4, x5).

The sender publishes three kinds of state. Closed CSs carry trailer state=closed. Green-checkpoint prefixes (PostToolUse of a configured check command) carry state=checkpoint seq=N, and receivers materialize them by default. At a 300 s cap, after T0 checks, the sender publishes state=wip, which receivers materialize only on opt-in. Claims still go out immediately as board-only pushes. Measured on real timings (x12): half-done exposure falls from 100% to 3%; edit-to-publish goes from p50 3 s to p50 96 s / p90 266 s; claims reach the board at p50 8 s; pushes stay at 2-3/min of the 6/min budget. This departs from decision 3's 'tens of seconds when busy'. Whether `publish: checkpoint` or `publish: live` (WIP visible, relying on the NOTE-1 records) is the default is the user's call.

Replace per-hunk push-gate withdrawal AND the PostToolUse restore with an all-or-nothing HOLD of the CS and of same-session dependent CSs. The author's disk keeps everything, and the hold is a board record that drives the requirement-4 'may I go first?' negotiation. On the sender, a hold pins whole FILES at their last-published blob, and any other work on that PC that lands in those files is held with it, so no hunk is ever subtracted from a file. Reason: x2 and x4a publish trees that never existed and break every peer while the sender stays green. x3b and x4b show that -U0 withdrawal inside a file duplicates or deletes functions, breaks C# syntax, and even alters non-foreign symbols.

Reconcile with the git-integrity proposal of per-path tolerant apply (M' = M with pending paths from S). Keep the tree surgery, but compute the pending set as the closure over CS membership: all paths of every incoming CS that touches a locked, fenced, invalid or colliding path. Preflight writability, and roll back the CS closure if read-tree fails partway. CS membership travels in code-commit trailers (Cowork-CS: ...), not only on the board, so it stays atomic with the tree even without --atomic.

Save never synthesizes a tree. It walks back from the live tip over up to 20 existing live commits and runs the configured smoke check on each in a throwaway worktree (about 0.5 s for 3k files, plus the check). It saves the newest passing commit with no open or wip CS, otherwise the newest passing commit, and refuses if none passes. Reason: x6a and x6b show that splicing out ACTIVE symbols, or even whole CSs, commits red trees while every PC is green.

Add a tiered check pipeline. T0 runs in-daemon on every publish in under 0.5 s: a parse check, symbol accounting, a caller-arity re-check for breaking signature changes after every merge and re-merge, and a guard against files becoming empty or shrinking sharply. T1 runs at checkpoints and at save: the configured import/build/test command. Reason: every Python break in this sweep passed py_compile (x1-x7, x13).

Treat Bash/PowerShell tool calls as transactions on both sides: no snapshot and no apply while one runs, with a 120 s cap, closed by PostToolUse, PostToolUseFailure or PermissionDenied. Add snapshot stability rules: fenced paths are not re-read; a change without hooks must be stable across two reads 1 s apart; a change from non-empty to empty needs attribution. Reason: x13 captured 5 empty blobs in 416 snapshots of an in-place writer.

Replace any time-windowed 'recent provenance, do not fix' rule with CS-keyed `incomplete` records (owner, affected paths and symbols, expected error signatures, resolves_when). A PostToolUseFailure hook on Bash/PowerShell and a PreToolUse hook on affected symbols inject them, and they live until the CS completes. Reason: blame of a withdrawal break points at base lines (x2), and deferral breaks exist only locally.

Add invariants next to INV-NOLOSS and INV-CONVERGE, which both pass in every scenario above. INV-ATOMIC-PUB: every live commit is base plus whole CSs, except declared prefixes (trailer state=checkpoint seq=N) and state=wip. INV-ATOMIC-APPLY: no disk holds a strict subset of a CS's paths unless the status shows it pending. INV-SAVE-RAN: a saved tree equals a live tree and passed the smoke check.
open_questions: This lens did not have the round-1 digest. How does the push gate define a 'hunk'? (This sweep assumed git -U0 hunks matched against symbol ranges.) Does withdrawal also revert the sender's disk? (Assumed not; the PostToolUse restore was treated as the disk-reverting variant.)

Is prompt_id present and fresh for turns that an inbox message starts on an idle session, and after /clear or compaction? Does Stop always fire for those turns? If not, the turn epoch must be driven by Stop/StopFailure plus UserPromptSubmit only.

Does Claude Code's Edit/Write write files in place (truncate + write) or via a temp file and rename? Both x13 results depend on it: the torn 0-byte snapshot, and the 511/824 Windows write failures (UNKNOWN -4094 while git had the file open). At realistic rates, can the daemon's reads make Claude's Edit fail on Windows? This needs the editor-fs lens.

Is a median code-visibility latency of about 1.5 min (checkpoint mode) acceptable to the team, given the promise of 'seconds when quiet'? Should `publish: live` be the default instead, with WIP visible plus incomplete records? This is the user's call.

Which commands count as a green checkpoint? The simulation optimistically counted every exit-0 Bash/PowerShell call. With a strict configured list (pytest, dotnet build, npm test) there are fewer checkpoints, so latency moves toward the hold-only (P1) numbers.
uvicorn --reload on Windows was not verified. In the headless harness it stalled at 'Reloading...' because its CTRL_C_EVENT restart needs a real console. Re-test in a real terminal.

Note for the git-integrity lens (VERIFIED in lib.py's first run): a temp index created with `read-tree <tree>` has no stat data. `read-tree -m -u` then refuses every path as 'not uptodate' until `update-index -q --refresh` runs, so a 'not uptodate, re-snapshot and retry' loop would spin forever. Seed the apply index from the snapshot index, or refresh it.
Simulation caveats: the timings come from this one user's 29 transcripts (1,901 editing turns), replayed on 4 simulated PCs, with assumed idle gaps of 20-120 s, no human edits and no CAS contention.

Save candidates: with 4 busy PCs, a live commit with no CS open anywhere is rare (turn p50 341 s vs 20-120 s idle), so SAVE-2 will usually save a checkpoint or wip state that passed the smoke check. Is that acceptable, or should save offer a short barrier that asks live sessions to reach Stop, with a timeout?

gapResults.lens: gap:Claude Code host-behavior assumptions that the mitigations depend on, and the aggregate usage/cost model

findings.title: Every PreToolUse gate failure mode lets the Edit through, and Claude never learns the gate was down
findings.evidence_detail: run1 (claude -p 2.1.270, Win11, sweep/host/run1.sh; transcript f1976867*.jsonl; logs sweep/host/proj/logs). The matrix used Write under matcher ^(Write|Edit)$, the same hook pipeline as Edit. Six Write calls ran through three PreToolUse hooks. (1) Exec-form command missing gave attachment hook_non_blocking_error 'Executable not found in $PATH', exitCode 1, and the file was written. (2) A node hook that throws (exit 1) was non-blocking; the file was written. (3) A hook sleeping past timeout:3 gave hook_cancelled timedOut:true durationMs 3103; the file was written. (4) An mcp_tool hook returning isError:true whose body was a deny JSON was non-blocking; the file was written. (5) Control: exit 2 blocked. (6) Control: mcp_tool deny JSON blocked. Binary 2.1.284 has hook_non_blocking_error:()=>[], so the error is never rendered to the model; the user sees only a one-line hook-error notice. DOCUMENTED: code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#other-exit-codes and #timeouts.
findings.scenario: 1. Alice starts /cowork start in a terminal where nvm puts node on PATH, and the per-user-per-repo daemon starts with an absolute node path. 2. Later Alice (or teammate Bob) opens Claude in VS Code. The extension host PATH has no node, or the plugin auto-updated and the bundle throws at load, or the MCP server crashed, or the daemon IPC stalls during a slow fetch. 3. In that session Claude edits parse_row(), which Younghee holds a PUBLISHED claim on. 4. The PreToolUse gate fails in one of the ways above. The Edit applies. Claude gets no signal; the user sees a grey 'PreToolUse:Edit hook error' line. 5. The running daemon snapshots and pushes the edit. Younghee's daemon then merges it into the function she is rewriting.
findings.consequence: Claims silently stop protecting anything. The holder's work-in-progress is overwritten or merged into, and the conflict-causer logic never fires because no deny happened. Round-1 mitigations this breaks: (1) 'Fail-closed exec-form node hook' is false for ENOENT, an uncaught exception, a timeout, isError, and a disconnected server. (2) 'Marker-file-keyed fail-closed gate' only gives deny-all-when-daemon-down from a hook that actually RAN; a hook that never ran denies nothing. (3) 'SessionStart node-presence preflight that disables live mode loudly' is itself an exec-form node hook, so it fails the same way when node is missing, and SessionStart errors show to the user only as a one-line notice, never to Claude. 'Loudly' needs a shell-form fallback (plain stdout becomes SessionStart context), or the daemon treating 'no armed seat' as the signal.
findings.mitigation: (a) The PreToolUse gate is ADVISORY. The only hard boundary is the daemon's PUBLISH GATE. Before each push, map every changed hunk in the snapshot to symbols. Each symbol must be covered by a claim this seat held before the change, per a ledger timestamped by the daemon. Uncovered and unconflicted symbols get a retro-claim. A hunk that conflicts with an earlier published claim is withheld: it goes to a local-only ref refs/cowork-local/quarantine/<seat> and is never pushed, and a notice goes into that seat's next hook context. (b) The hook entry file is a dependency-free loader. Its first line is process.on('uncaughtException',()=>process.exit(2)). It wraps require(bundle) in try/catch mapped to exit 2, and it has an internal deadline below the host timeout, so that everything except ENOENT and SIGKILL becomes a block. (c) Arming: a seat is ARMED only after a gate round-trip for that seat. A PostToolUse(Edit|Write) event or a working-tree change with no preceding gate call marks the seat UNARMED and quarantines its conflicting hunks. Use a second, command-type PostToolUse hook as the independent channel. (d) Set an explicit `timeout: 10` on gate hooks.
findings.test: Pin a Claude Code version and publish a conflicting claim from a fake peer. Inject each failure in turn: node removed from PATH, bundle syntax error, thrown exception, sleep longer than the timeout, MCP server killed, isError result. Assert three things: the local file changed (host behaviour, expected); the remote live ref never contains the hunk (git cat-file on refs/cowork/<b>/code); the quarantine ref does contain it, and the next PostToolUse additionalContext mentions it.

findings.title: Implementing requirement 4 literally (all Claudes notice and warn) multiplies full-context idle wakes across 4 accounts
findings.evidence_detail: costs.md#why-usage-climbs: a cross-session message to an idle session 'starts a new turn ... sending your full context each time'. cross-session-messaging.md: 'counts toward usage like a prompt'. The host only drops IDENTICAL repeats and refuses bursts; distinct messages keep flowing. Measured baseline on this PC (460 active main-thread hours): median context per request is 511k tokens (p10 148k, p90 899k). The run1 floor is about 30k tokens per request.
findings.scenario: 1. Chulsoo's Claude edits a symbol inside Younghee's propagation window, and board order makes Chulsoo the causer. 2. The daemons of the 3 non-causers each push 'conflict by Chulsoo' into their own idle sessions: 3 wakes. 3. Each of those Claudes composes a warning through a cowork tool, which reaches Chulsoo's session as 3 distinct messages: 1-3 more wakes. 4. Chulsoo's Claude asks 'may I go first?', which wakes the holder. The holder's Stop hook asks, it answers, and its daemon broadcasts the decision, which wakes the others again. 5. Repeat for each conflict.
findings.consequence: One conflict costs about 8 wakes x 2-3 requests x 511k, roughly 8-12M input tokens. At 6 conflicts/h that is 25-70M tokens/h across the team, about 1-2x a median active hour (29.5M), much of it burned while people are away. A wake after the 1 h cache TTL (5 min on API keys) re-writes the whole cache: 12-20x the cost of a warm wake. Wake-reply cascades between 4 Claudes are distinct messages, so the host throttles never stop them.
findings.mitigation: (a) The causer's OWN daemon computes the warning deterministically from board order and delivers it once to the causer: O(1) wakes per conflict, not O(N). The other seats get one digest line at their next natural tool call or prompt and are never woken. (b) Per-seat wake budget: at most 1 per 5 min and at most 4 per hour, coalesced into one message. (c) Never wake a seat whose last UserPromptSubmit is more than 10 min old, or whose last response is older than the prompt-cache TTL; hold until the next prompt. (d) A turn that a wake started can never cause another wake-class message: no cascades. (e) A team-wide wake budget lives in the board, and over budget everything degrades to digest mode.
findings.test: 4-seat simulation with real sessions or a stub inbox. Script 6 conflicts in 10 min. Count inbox deliveries per seat. Assert: deliveries per conflict ≤ 2 (causer + holder); 0 deliveries to seats idle for more than 10 min; no message whose causal chain includes a wake-originated turn. In interactive sessions, compare /usage before and after.

findings.title: Write is refused if a peer change lands between Read and Write; PreToolUse never fires, so the file fence cannot help and Claude loops on re-Read
findings.evidence_detail: In-session test (2.1.284) and run1 (2.1.270). After an external change, Write returned 'File has been modified since read, either by the user or by a linter. Read it again before attempting to write it.' The run1 hooklog has NO PreToolUse and NO PostToolUseFailure entry for the refused tool_use. The retry succeeded only because Read->Write took about 2 s while the writer cadence was 5 s. DOCUMENTED (tools-reference#write-tool-behavior): files read only partially (PARTIAL view) need a full read before Write, so the 1.3 MB file can never be Written at all.
findings.scenario: 1. Claude fully Reads routes.js (400 lines) and spends about 40 s generating a full-file Write. 2. The daemon applies Younghee's change to routes.js during generation. The fence is not engaged, because a fence starts at PreToolUse, which comes after generation. 3. Write is refused before any hook runs. 4. Claude re-Reads (+5k tokens of context, kept) and regenerates (+5k OUTPUT tokens). Each attempt is refused with probability 1-exp(-40/10), about 98%, while the file stays hot.
findings.consequence: Agent loops: repeated full-file regeneration (output tokens cost about 5x input), context bloat, and a Write that never lands. The error tells Claude the change came from 'the user or a linter', so Claude may believe its own user is editing concurrently.
findings.mitigation: Read lease: a PostToolUse(Read) hook reports (seat, path, offset/limit, content hash) to the daemon. While a full-read lease is live (120 s, or until that seat's next Edit/Write PostToolUse on the path; at most 3 renewals; at most 5 min total), the apply step HOLDS that path. It builds MERGED' = MERGED with held paths taken from the current local tree and keeps the incoming change pending for the next cycle. SessionStart context also says 'in cowork mode prefer Edit over Write for existing files'.
findings.test: Harness: the daemon applies a peer change to f.js every 5 s. A scripted session does Read f.js, waits 6 s, then Write f.js. Without the lease, the refusal reproduces. With the lease, the first Write succeeds, and after the next cycle the file contains both Claude's content and the peer change (3-way merged).

findings.title: Claude Code's changed-file reminder tells Claude that peer WIP is deliberate current state and not to call it out
findings.evidence_detail: Exact framing in the 2.1.270 and 2.1.284 binaries: 'Note: <file> changed on disk since you last read it. That's usually deliberate, so take it as the current state rather than reverting it; if the change looks wrong, say so rather than undoing it yourself — otherwise no need to call it out. Here are the relevant changes (shown with line numbers):'. The generator (same binaries) iterates readFileState. It SKIPS reads that had offset/limit, and reads truncated by the token cap. It emits diff hunks with 8 context lines, with a snippet budget of 16,384 chars per step; beyond that the snippet is blank and the file is dropped from readFileState. Real transcripts on this PC (claude-vscode, 60 newest sessions) contain 560 such reminders: 77% injected mid-turn after a tool result, snippet median 5.8k chars, p90 8.2k. Negative result: 2 claude -p runs (2.1.270), one with 4 turns, produced 0 reminders although the fully-read med.py changed every 5 s, so the reminder depends on the entrypoint.
findings.scenario: 1. Bob's Claude has fully read utils.py (900 lines). 2. Younghee's Claude is half-way through changing load_rows(path) to load_rows(path, enc) and has not updated the callers yet. Her claim is published. The daemon applies her change to Bob's tree. 3. On Bob's next step the reminder shows the hunk and says 'usually deliberate ... take it as the current state ... no need to call it out'. 4. Bob's Claude adapts its new code to the half-done signature, or 'completes' the rename by fixing callers, some of them inside Younghee's claimed area. It does not tell Bob that a teammate changed this file.
findings.consequence: Agents build on or finish teammates' unfinished work, spread WIP signatures into unrelated code, and stay silent about it. The 1.3 MB / 26k-line file is never reminded (it can only be read with offset/limit), so Claude's view of it goes stale with no notice at all. Edits based on stale line numbers or bodies then fail with 'not found', which forces 25k-token page re-reads.
findings.mitigation: Attribution channel. The daemon journals every apply: path, line ranges, symbol, peer, whether the claim is still held. Every PostToolUse hook (all tools) returns additionalContext listing the peer changes applied, since the previous tool call, to files this seat has read (full or ranged). The text is factual and third-person, at most 600 chars, coalesced, for example: 'cowork-sync: lines 120-160 of utils.py (load_rows) were changed by teammate Younghee's session, which still holds the claim (work in progress, not requested by your user).' SessionStart context states the standing rule: code in symbols claimed by others is someone else's WIP; do not extend or complete it; build against the last saved version or file a cowork request.
findings.test: A/B evaluation in an INTERACTIVE harness (terminal under ConPTY, or VS Code), since -p does not emit the reminder. A peer applies a half-done signature change to a fully read file. Run 20 times with the attribution note and 20 without. Measure the % of runs in which Claude edits the claimed symbol or adopts the WIP signature, and the % in which it tells the user. Target: edits ≤5%, mentions ≥80%. Also assert that an edited_text_file attachment appears in the transcript, which proves the reminder fired.

findings.title: Per-step changed-file reminders accumulate in 1M-context sessions, and the cost grows each hour
findings.evidence_detail: Reminder rules come from the binaries: one per changed fully-read file per step, up to 16,384 chars per step. Rates are from transcripts on this PC: solo median 60 requests/active hour (p90 154), reminder size median 5.8k chars (about 1.7k tokens), solo rate 1.08 per active hour (max 26), median context 511k, so compaction rarely triggers. The cowork rate is REASONED from team cadence.
findings.scenario: 1. 4 peers; team pushes about 1 per 10 s, so each seat receives about 270 applies/h. 2. Bob's session has 6 small or medium files fully read that peers are editing. 3. About 50 of Bob's 60 steps per hour carry a reminder of about 1.7k tokens. 4. The reminders stay in context and are re-sent on every later request.
findings.consequence: Hour 1 adds about 50 x 1.7k x 30 (average remaining requests) ≈ 2.5M cache-read tokens. Every further hour adds about 85k tokens x 60 ≈ 5M more, growing linearly until compaction. With 200k-window users it instead forces compaction every 1-2 h, and each compaction is a full-context request plus a 10-20k-token summary output.
findings.mitigation: (a) The read lease from write-staleness-check-precedes-hooks also defers applies to files that a seat is actively editing. (b) Per-seat cadence: while a seat is mid-turn (hook traffic within the last 60 s), apply changes to its fully-read files at most once per 2 min, coalesced into one diff. (c) Per-seat budget: when the estimated reminder volume (the daemon knows the applied diff sizes for files in the seat's read set) exceeds 20k chars/hour, switch the seat to pull mode, which applies to read files only at Stop or UserPromptSubmit. Report the estimate in /cowork status.
findings.test: 30-min interactive soak with synthetic peer churn on 6 read files. Count edited_text_file attachments and the sum of their snippet chars in the transcript JSONL. Assert ≤15 reminders and ≤20k chars per hour, and that no peer change is lost (all present after Stop).

findings.title: Real-time delivery silently stops for bypassPermissions or plan-mode receivers, crossSessionInbound hold/refuse, --bare, and older Windows builds
findings.evidence_detail: cross-session-messaging.md: when no crossSessionInbound value applies, a receiver that bypasses permission prompts HOLDS each message unless it is a verified own-child; on native Windows the token in the auth line is the only verification. Plan mode with bypass available counts as bypassing. Held dialogs expire after 5 min and the message is dropped. At most 100 held messages, oldest dropped; at most 50 queued. 'refuse' in project/local settings overrides everything. --bare binds no socket. costs.md recommends setting 'hold' to save usage. VERIFIED (run1): the stdio MCP server's env holds its own session's CLAUDE_CODE_MESSAGING_SOCKET (\\.\pipe\LOCAL\cc-msg-299b...) and a 32-char token, identical to the SessionStart hook env, with the outer session's vars unset. So daemon -> MCP child -> socket can authenticate as own-child, but the detached daemon (not a child) cannot.
findings.scenario: 1. Chulsoo runs in bypassPermissions, or set crossSessionInbound: hold after reading the cost docs. 2. Bob's blocked edit produces 'Bob requests parse_row: quick fix, may I go first?' for Chulsoo. 3. The message is held as an approval dialog. Chulsoo is away, so it expires after 5 min and is dropped. 4. Bob's Claude is told 'asked, waiting for reply' and waits, or keeps re-asking.
findings.consequence: Requirement 4 fails with no error on either side. Blocked work stalls, and a design that assumes 'nothing is ever lost' loses the ask if the inbox was the carrier.
findings.mitigation: (a) The inbox is a doorbell only. Every request lives in the board with an id and a deadline, and Claude fetches it through an MCP tool. (b) At SessionStart, compute each seat's delivery state (live, held or off) from: messaging env present, Claude Code version, permission_mode from the hook input, and the effective crossSessionInbound from the settings files. Publish it in the board. (c) A requester whose target is held or off is told 'not reachable live; queued as R17; shown at their next prompt'. (d) Only the MCP server posts to its own session's socket, with the token from its own env. Scrub CLAUDE_CODE_MESSAGING_* from the daemon env.
findings.test: Matrix test. Receiver permission modes: default, acceptEdits, auto, bypassPermissions, plan. crossSessionInbound: unset, accept, hold, refuse. Assert the board delivery state is correct in every cell, and that the request reaches the holder's context by the next UserPromptSubmit/PostToolUse digest even when the doorbell was held or dropped.

findings.title: The detached daemon escapes the job object and outlives claude, /plugin disable, and plugin updates; it carries a stale inherited environment
findings.evidence_detail: run1: a node child spawned detached (stdio ignore, windowsHide) from a SessionStart exec-form hook did not delay the session. IsProcessInJob was False for the daemon, while claude.exe and the MCP server node were inJob=True. tasklist showed the daemon alive and heartbeating for more than 60 s after claude -p exited. The hook env, and so the daemon env, contained the session's CLAUDE_CODE_MESSAGING_SOCKET/TOKEN, and here VS Code vars such as ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 and GIT_EDITOR=true. DOCUMENTED in runtime-dist.md: old CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT versions are swept 14 days after being orphaned. Survival of an interactive /exit is REASONED: the parent has exited and the process is not in a job, so tree and job kills cannot reach it.
findings.scenario: 1. A daemon starts from Alice's session. 2. Alice runs /plugin disable cowork-sync, or the plugin auto-updates. No disable hook exists. 3. The old daemon keeps fetching, merging peers' work into her working tree and pushing her edits, with no gate, no MCP server and no UI. 4. Weeks later the old plugin root is swept. Lazily loaded assets (the C# tree-sitter WASM, 5.35 MB) now fail with ENOENT, so mapping degrades to whole-file or none. 5. If the first session had GIT_DIR or GIT_INDEX_FILE set (for example, Claude launched from a git hook or exec), the daemon's plumbing inherits it.
findings.consequence: Invisible sync after the user believes cowork is off. Peers' changes keep landing in her tree and her edits keep publishing. Version skew between the daemon and the hooks. A risk of writing the user's real index.
findings.mitigation: (a) Lease-based lifetime. The daemon applies and pushes only while at least one seat lease is valid: an MCP server heartbeat every 15 s, or an explicit human lease from the CLI with an expiry. With no lease for 2 min, it stops syncing; after 10 min it exits. (b) Version handshake on each MCP connect. On a mismatch, the old daemon drains, exits, and is respawned from the new version. (c) At start, copy all runtime assets to CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA/runtime/<version>/ and load every grammar eagerly. (d) Spawn with an env ALLOWLIST: PATH, SystemRoot, USERPROFILE/HOME, TEMP, LANG, plus explicitly configured git credential vars. Drop CLAUDE_*, GIT_*, ELECTRON_*, VSCODE_*.
findings.test: (1) Start a session, kill all MCP servers (or disable the plugin): no push after 2 min, process gone after 10 min (tasklist/ps). (2) Bump the plugin version: the old daemon exits within 30 s. (3) Start claude with GIT_INDEX_FILE=<tmp> set: the daemon's git calls never open that file (checked via procmon/strace or a canary hash).

findings.title: After a gate deny, Claude may finish the job through Bash or PowerShell writes, which PreToolUse(Edit) never sees
findings.evidence_detail: DOCUMENTED (hooks: Bash/PowerShell are separate tools, and bashEditDiff is best-effort, beta, and recorded only in auto/bypass mode unless bashEditDiffEnabled is set). The agent behaviour is reasoned from goal-directed models that route around a blocked tool. It was not measured here.
findings.scenario: 1. The gate denies Bob's Edit on parse_row. 2. Bob's Claude, told to finish the task, runs `python -c "...replace..."` or PowerShell Set-Content on hub.py. 3. No Edit hook fires. The daemon snapshots and publishes the change into Younghee's claimed function.
findings.consequence: Claims are bypassed by the very agent that was blocked. The 'conflict causer' record never exists, because the deny looked like it worked.
findings.mitigation: (a) The publish gate and quarantine from gate-fails-open-on-every-hook-failure catch it regardless. (b) The deny reason says, factually: 'The change was recorded as request R17 for the holder; edits to this function by any means are withheld from sync until the claim is released.' (c) A PreToolUse(Bash|PowerShell) advisory hook warns when the command string names a file with claimed symbols.
findings.test: 20 scripted runs where the user prompt insists on completing a denied change. Count runs with a Bash or PowerShell write to the file. Assert the live ref never contains the hunk (quarantined) in 20/20, and that the workaround rate drops with the reworded deny reason.
